use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ExceptionEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Generator\UrlGeneratorInterface;
use Twig\Environment;

#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::EXCEPTION, priority: -10)]
class ErrorPage
{
    public function __construct(
        private Environment $twig,
        private Flash $flash,
        private UrlGeneratorInterface $urls,
        // the debug mode (APP_ENV=dev): the kernel.debug parameter of the container
        #[Autowire('%kernel.debug%')] private bool $debug,
    ) {
    }

    public function __invoke(ExceptionEvent $event): void
    {
        $e = $event->getThrowable();

        if ($e instanceof InvalidSession) {
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
            $event->setResponse(AuthService::clearCookie(new RedirectResponse($this->urls->generate('login'))));
            return;
        }

        if ($e instanceof HttpExceptionInterface) {
            $event->setResponse($this->page($e->getStatusCode()));
            return;
        }

        // a real anomaly: in development, Symfony's debug page
        if (! $this->debug) {
            $event->setResponse($this->page(500));
        }
    }

    // the error page, with the HTTP code of the error and its message
    private function page(int $code): Response
    {
        $message = match ($code) {
            400 => 'ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST',
            403 => 'ERRORS.FORBIDDEN',
            404, 405 => 'ERRORS.NOT_FOUND',
            419 => 'ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED',
            default => 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
        };
        return new Response($this->twig->render('error.html.twig', ['pageTitle' => 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE',
            'code' => $code, 'message' => $message]), $code);
    }
}

How Errors Become Pages HTML: This is the listener [ErrorPage] from Example 24, expanded. It listens for the event [kernel.exception], with priority -10 (line 37): after the [Symfony] listener, which logs the exception (priority 0), and after the security component’s listener (priority 1), which converts an access denial either into a call to the entry point (anonymous visitor) or into a 403 error (authenticated user with an inappropriate role); before the handler that generates the error page, [Symfony] (-128). Three cases:

  • lines 53–57: a [InvalidSession] (the account has been deleted): the “session expired” message, deletion of the token cookie, and the login page;
  • lines 59–62: a HTTP error: [HttpExceptionInterface] is the exception handler for exceptions with the code HTTP ([NotFoundHttpException], [AccessDeniedHttpException], [HttpException(419)]...), which is thrown by [getStatusCode]. The error page is displayed, showing this code;
  • lines 65–67: another exception is a true error. In development ([kernel.debug], example 24), the listener does nothing: the debug page for [Symfony], showing the call stack, will be displayed. In production, the 500 error page: the user never sees the call stack, which the log has already captured;
  • lines 71–82: the error page, view [error.html.twig], showing the message code and key. [match] ([PHP] 8) selects a value based on another, using strict equality; [404, 405 =>] covers two cases; [default] handles all others. Code 405 (Method Not Allowed: a GET on an address that only accepts POST) is displayed as a "page not found" error.

docs.title: 11.14.1. src/Controller/AuthController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/AuthController.php: the PUBLIC routes of the login:
//   GET  /        redirects to the home page of the role (or to /login)
//   GET  /login   displays the login form (with its captcha)
//   POST /login   checks attempt limit, captcha, login / password
//   POST /logout  the logout
//
// Protection against robots, in this order:
//   1. too many recent failures for this login from this IP address?
//      -> immediate refusal, without even looking at the password;
//   2. wrong answer to the captcha? -> refusal (counted as a failure);
//   3. only then, check of the password.
// We NEVER check the password of an attempt refused at steps 1 or 2:
// a robot can therefore learn nothing by insisting.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Role;
use App\Security\AuthService;
use App\Security\CaptchaService;
use App\Security\AttemptLimiter;
use App\Security\ConnectedUser;
use App\Web\BaseController;
use App\Web\Message;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class AuthController extends BaseController
{
    public function __construct(
        private AuthService $auth,
        private CaptchaService $captchas,
        private AttemptLimiter $limiter,
    ) {
    }

    // the home page of each role, right after the login: the name of its route
    public static function homePage(Role $role): string
    {
        return $role === Role::USER ? 'area' : 'schedule';
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /
    // The route is public: the user, if there is one, is known
    // ($this->getUser()), but nothing is required.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/', name: 'home', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function home(): Response
    {
        $user = $this->getUser();
        return $this->redirectToRoute($user instanceof ConnectedUser
            ? self::homePage($user->role) : 'login');
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the login field
    // (used right after the creation of an account, see RegistrationController)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/login', name: 'login', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function form(Request $request): Response
    {
        // already logged in (token still valid): straight to the home page
        $user = $this->getUser();
        if ($user instanceof ConnectedUser) {
            return $this->redirectToRoute(self::homePage($user->role));
        }
        // mb_substr: 30 characters at most
        return $this->page(mb_substr($request->query->getString('login'), 0, 30), null);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /login
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/login', name: 'login_submit', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function logIn(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        $login = $request->request->getString('login');
        $password = $request->request->getString('password');
        $ip = (string) $request->getClientIp();

        // 1. too many recent failures?
        $minutes = $this->limiter->loginBlockMinutes($ip, $login);
        if ($minutes > 0) {
            return $this->page($login, new Message('ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', ['minutes' => $minutes]));
        }

        // 2. the captcha
        if (! $this->captchas->verify($request->request->getString('captchaId'),
            $request->request->getString('captcha'))) {
            $this->limiter->loginFailure($ip, $login);
            return $this->page($login, new Message('ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA'));
        }

        // 3. the password
        $user = $login !== '' && $password !== '' ? $this->auth->validate($login, $password) : null;
        if ($user === null) {
            $this->limiter->loginFailure($ip, $login);
            return $this->page($login, new Message('LOGIN.ERROR'));
        }

        $this->limiter->loginSuccess($ip, $login);
        $response = $this->redirectToRoute(self::homePage($user->getRole()));
        $response->headers->setCookie($this->auth->tokenCookie($user));
        return $response;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /logout: clear the token cookie, then go to the login page.
    // POST only: a simple link (GET), placed on another site, cannot
    // log the user out without their knowledge.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/logout', name: 'logout', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function logOut(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        return AuthService::clearCookie($this->redirectToRoute('login'));
    }

    // the form, always with a NEW captcha (each image is used only
    // once); the entered login is displayed again, never the password. An error:
    // the code 422, as for an invalid form (see example 19)
    private function page(string $login, ?Message $error): Response
    {
        return $this->render('login.html.twig', ['pageTitle' => 'LOGIN.TITLE', 'error' => $error,
            'login' => $login, 'captcha' => $this->captchas->generate()],
            new Response(status: $error ? 422 : 200));
    }
}

The login controller, which is based on Example 27. It inherits from the application’s [BaseController] class (discussed later), which itself is a subclass of [AbstractController].

  • lines 41–44: the home page for each role, along with its route name: “My area” for a patient, and the calendar for others;
  • lines 51–57: The address [/] links to the role’s home page or to the login page. The route is public (rule [access_control] of [security.yaml]): [getUser()] returns the user established by the authenticator, if there is one, without requiring anything. [redirectToRoute] (example 04) creates a redirect to a named route;
  • lines 63–73: a user who is already logged in goes directly to their home page. The optional parameter [login] of URL pre-fills the field (after account creation); [mb_substr] truncates it to 30 characters;
  • Lines 78–110: the login process, in the order shown in Example 27: the anti-CSRF token (discussed later), any blocking measures, the CAPTCHA, and the password. A password is never verified for an attempt rejected by the limiter or the CAPTCHA: a bot learns nothing by persisting. [getClientIp] returns the client’s address IP. If the attempt fails, the page is rendered directly (no redirection): the re-displayed form always has a new CAPTCHA and the entered login. The error is an object [Message] (see below), consisting of a key and its parameters, displayed at the bottom of the page. If successful, the login counter is reset to zero, and the browser is redirected to the role’s home page, with the token cookie ([headers->setCookie]);
  • lines 117–122: Logout deletes the token cookie (example 25). It only accepts POST, along with the anti-CSRF token: a simple link placed on another site cannot log the user out without their knowledge;
  • lines 127–132: the login page. The third parameter of [render] is the response to be populated: an error is returned with code 422 (Unprocessable Content), as with an invalid form (example 19). [new Response(status: ...)] uses a named argument ([PHP] 8): the first two parameters of the constructor retain their default values.

The login page receives the variable [pageTitle], the translation key for the page title: all actions pass it to their view for the template (see below).

docs.title: 11.15. The Web Layer: Shared Services
docs.text: The [src/Web] folder contains the elements shared by the controllers.

docs.title: 11.15.1. src/Web/ApplicationModel.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/ApplicationModel.php: the cache / facade of the business layer (the equivalent
// of the [ApplicationModel] class of the other versions of the application): the
// lists of doctors and clients are read from the database once, then served from
// the cache.
//
// Why Symfony's CACHE, and not simply a property of this object? Because
// a PHP application keeps nothing in memory from one request to the next: this
// object is a shared service, but a service only lives for ONE request.
// The cache, on the other hand, is shared by all the requests (see examples 20 and 23).
//
// These lists may CHANGE (the ADMIN adds, modifies, deletes doctors and
// clients): each write therefore goes through this facade, which FORGETS the list
// concerned right afterwards; the next request that needs it reads it again from the database. That is
// the whole point of a SINGLE entry point to the business layer: the rule
// "write => cache update" is written only here.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use App\Domain\DoctorDaySchedule;
use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Slot;
use App\Entity\Doctor;
use App\Entity\Appointment;
use App\Business\PersonData;
use App\Business\Business;
use App\Business\BusinessService;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use Symfony\Contracts\Cache\CacheInterface;

// same contract as the business layer
class ApplicationModel implements Business
{
    private const DOCTORS = 'rdvmedecins.doctors';

    private const CLIENTS = 'rdvmedecins.clients';

    // CacheInterface: the cache of the application (the cache.app service), seen through
    // the interface of Symfony's "contracts", simpler than that of PSR-6
    public function __construct(private BusinessService $business, private CacheInterface $cache)
    {
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

    // get(key, function): the value of the cache if it exists; otherwise, the function
    // is called, and its result stored in the cache (without time limit) before
    // being returned. The entities are stored there serialized (see serialize): each
    // request that reads them gets copies of them, which Doctrine does not track
    public function getAllDoctors(): array
    {
        return $this->cache->get(self::DOCTORS, fn () => $this->business->getAllDoctors());
    }

    public function getAllClients(): array
    {
        return $this->cache->get(self::CLIENTS, fn () => $this->business->getAllClients());
    }

    // the doctor whose user account is [$userId] - used to preselect,
    // for a logged-in doctor, their own schedule. array_find: the first element
    // of the array that satisfies the condition (null if there is none)
    public function getDoctorByUserId(int $userId): ?Doctor
    {
        return array_find($this->getAllDoctors(), fn (Doctor $d) => $d->getAccount()->getId() === $userId);
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    public function getAllSlots(int $doctorId): array
    {
        return $this->business->getAllSlots($doctorId);
    }

    public function getDoctorDayAppointments(int $doctorId, DateTimeImmutable $day): array
    {
        return $this->business->getDoctorDayAppointments($doctorId, $day);
    }

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client
    {
        return $this->business->getClientById($id);
    }

    public function getDoctorById(int $id): ?Doctor
    {
        return $this->business->getDoctorById($id);
    }

    public function getAppointmentById(int $id): ?Appointment
    {
        return $this->business->getAppointmentById($id);
    }

    public function getSlotById(int $id): ?Slot
    {
        return $this->business->getSlotById($id);
    }

    public function getDoctorDaySchedule(int $doctorId, DateTimeImmutable $day): ?DoctorDaySchedule
    {
        return $this->business->getDoctorDaySchedule($doctorId, $day);
    }

    // no cache here: it is the most recent data that matters (a patient who
    // has just modified or deleted their account)
    public function getClientByUserId(int $userId): ?Client
    {
        return $this->business->getClientByUserId($userId);
    }

    public function getClientUpcomingAppointments(int $clientId): array
    {
        return $this->business->getClientUpcomingAppointments($clientId);
    }

    public function addAppointment(DateTimeImmutable $day, Slot $slot, Client $client): Appointment
    {
        return $this->business->addAppointment($day, $slot, $client);
    }

    public function deleteAppointment(Appointment $appointment): void
    {
        $this->business->deleteAppointment($appointment);
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------ writes => cache forgotten
    // (delete: the item is removed from the cache)

    public function addDoctor(PersonData $data): Doctor
    {
        $doctor = $this->business->addDoctor($data);
        $this->cache->delete(self::DOCTORS);
        return $doctor;
    }

    public function editDoctor(int $id, PersonData $data): Doctor
    {
        $doctor = $this->business->editDoctor($id, $data);
        $this->cache->delete(self::DOCTORS);
        return $doctor;
    }

    public function deleteDoctor(int $id): void
    {
        $this->business->deleteDoctor($id);
        $this->cache->delete(self::DOCTORS);
    }

    public function addClient(PersonData $data): Client
    {
        $client = $this->business->addClient($data);
        $this->cache->delete(self::CLIENTS);
        return $client;
    }

    public function editClient(int $id, PersonData $data): Client
    {
        $client = $this->business->editClient($id, $data);
        $this->cache->delete(self::CLIENTS);
        return $client;
    }

    public function deleteClient(int $id): void
    {
        $this->business->deleteClient($id);
        $this->cache->delete(self::CLIENTS);
    }
}

All versions of the application have a class named [ApplicationModel]: a single entry point from the web layer to the business layer, which keeps the lists of doctors and clients in memory. These lists are accessed by almost all pages (the drop-down list of doctors in the calendar, the list of patients in the booking window, and the administration pages) and rarely change.

What changes in [PHP] is the meaning of “in memory.” An application such as [Java], [C#], or [Python] remains in memory between requests; the [Flask] version stored these lists in the properties of a single object created at startup. An application [PHP] is recreated with each request (Example 01): the object [ApplicationModel] is indeed a shared service, but it exists only for the duration of a single request (Example 23). The lists are therefore stored in the cache of [Symfony] (example 20), which is shared by all requests.

  • Line 34: The class implements the [Business] interface, just like [BusinessService]: the controllers call the same methods, regardless of which class serves them;
  • Line 42: This time, the cache is received via the [CacheInterface] interface of the “contracts” for [Symfony] (the same [cache.app] service), which is simpler than the PSR-6 interface in the examples;
  • Lines 52–60: [get(key, function)] returns the value stored under this key; if it does not exist, it calls the function (which reads the list from the database), stores its result in the cache indefinitely, and returns it. The first query that needs the list reads it directly from the database; subsequent queries find it in the cache. The cache stores the array of entities in a serialized form (example 20) and reconstructs it upon reading, along with the loaded relationships (each person’s account). The reconstructed entities are copies that the [Doctrine] entity manager does not track: they are used for display, never for writing (the business layer always re-reads from the database what it modifies);
  • lines 65–68: the physician associated with an account, retrieved from the cache list by [array_find] (example 06);
  • Lines 72–127: The other methods of the [Business] contract simply delegate to the business layer. An account’s client ([getClientByUserId]) is always retrieved from the database, not from the cache: the most recent data takes precedence (a patient who has just modified or deleted their account);
  • Lines 132–170: the updates. Each update made by a doctor or a client does not save the relevant list ([delete]): the next query that needs it will retrieve it from the database. This is the whole point of a single entry point: the rule “a write updates the cache” is implemented only here. If the write fails (e.g., a [BusinessException]), the list is not overwritten—it hasn’t changed. An application that writes to the database via a different path (another program, another version of the application using the same database) would leave the cache out of date: [php bin/console cache:pool:clear cache.app] would clear it.

docs.title: 11.15.2. src/Web/Message.php and Flash.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Web/Message.php: a message to translate: its key, and its parameters.
// The views display it with {{ message.key|trans(message.params) }}.

namespace App\Web;

readonly class Message
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $key,
        public array $params = [],
    ) {
    }
}

A message to be translated: a key and its parameters. Errors in the business layer ([BusinessException]) and those in the controllers become [Message], which the views translate into the page’s language.

<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/Flash.php: the "flash" messages: a message to display ONCE, on the
// NEXT page (see example 20). It is the natural complement of the
// "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern used by all the forms of the application: a
// successful POST builds no page, it redirects (302) to a GET page; the
// message, on the other hand, must survive the redirection.
//
// Symfony stores them in the SESSION (files of the var/sessions folder, see
// config/packages/framework.yaml).
//
// A message does not contain a text, but a translation KEY and its parameters
// (a Message object): it is translated when displayed, in the language of
// the page (see templates/fragments). Two lists: the successes (displayed at the top of
// the page) and the errors (displayed at the bottom).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;

class Flash
{
    // the stack of requests, to reach the session of the current request
    public function __construct(private RequestStack $requests)
    {
    }

    public function success(string $key, array $params = []): void
    {
        $this->add('success', $key, $params);
    }

    public function error(string $key, array $params = []): void
    {
        $this->add('errors', $key, $params);
    }

    // getFlashBag: the "bag" of the flash messages of the session; add(type, message)
    // adds a message to the list of that type (see example 20)
    private function add(string $type, string $key, array $params): void
    {
        $this->requests->getSession()->getFlashBag()->add($type, new Message($key, $params));
    }
}

Flash messages (example 20): a message placed in the session by an action, displayed by the next page, then discarded. This complements the Post/Redirect/Get pattern, which all forms in the application follow. There are two types: success messages are displayed at the top of the page, and error messages at the bottom.

  • Line 25: the request stack ([RequestStack]), a service of [Symfony] that knows the current request and, therefore, its session. A shared service cannot receive the request itself via its constructor: it is created once and may be used for multiple requests (a main request and its sub-requests);
  • lines 41–44: the “bag” of session flash messages ([getFlashBag]), for which [add(type, message)] completes the list of this type. This is what the [addFlash] method of [AbstractController] does (Example 20); making it a service allows a message to be placed outside a controller—such as the authenticator or listeners.

The [Message] objects are stored as-is in the session: [PHP] serializes the session data (Example 20) and reconstructs it on the next request. In the views, [app.flashes('errors')] renders the list of messages of this type and removes them from the session.

docs.title: 11.15.3. src/Web/BaseController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/BaseController.php: the parent class of the controllers of the application. It
// inherits from AbstractController (see example 03), and adds the check of the
// anti-CSRF token of the hand-written forms (see example 21).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpException;

abstract class BaseController extends AbstractController
{
    // the identifier of the anti-CSRF token of the hand-written forms: only one
    // for the whole application (in the views: csrf_token('rdvmedecins')). The
    // forms of the Form component each have their own
    public const CSRF = 'rdvmedecins';

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // a missing or wrong anti-CSRF token: the page was probably displayed before
    // the expiry of the session, which contained the token. Error 419, the (unofficial,
    // but widespread) code of an expired page: the ErrorPage listener displays
    // "The page has expired: reload it, then try again."
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    protected function checkCsrf(Request $request): void
    {
        if (! $this->isCsrfTokenValid(self::CSRF, $request->request->getString('_token'))) {
            throw new HttpException(419, 'invalid anti-CSRF token');
        }
    }
}

The parent class for controllers. Forms written manually in the views (login, logout, deletions, reservations, etc.) include an anti-CSRF token (Example 21) with the identifier [rdvmedecins]: a single identifier is sufficient here, since all these actions already require a logged-in user or a CAPTCHA. Each form in the Form component has its own token, which is validated by the component.

A missing or invalid token stops the action with a 419 error (lines 27–32), the (unofficial but widely used) code for a page that has expired: the token is stored in the session, and a page displayed before the end of the session contains a token that the server no longer recognizes. The [ErrorPage] listener then displays “The page has expired: reload it, then try again.” [HttpException] is the generic exception HTTP: its constructor receives the code and a message (intended for the log, not for the user).

docs.title: 11.15.4. src/Web/Utils.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/Utils.php: small utility functions of the web layer:
//   - dates: "yyyy-mm-dd", days "Wednesday 23 September 2026";
//   - input: reading of a positive integer, of a date, sent by the browser;
//   - user: the logged-in user, and their patient (Client entity).
// The STATIC methods are called without an object (Utils::iso($day)); the others
// need services (the current request, security...): the class is a
// service, which the controllers receive through their constructor.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Security\InvalidSession;
use App\Security\ConnectedUser;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use IntlDateFormatter;
use Symfony\Bundle\SecurityBundle\Security;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;

class Utils
{
    // Security: Symfony's security service, which knows the user of
    // the current request (the one established by the authenticator)
    public function __construct(
        private RequestStack $requests,
        private Security $security,
        private ApplicationModel $application,
    ) {
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- dates

    // the date, if [$text] is a date that exists in the yyyy-mm-dd format; null otherwise.
    // createFromFormat accepts "2026-02-30" (which becomes March 2): we therefore
    // check that the date read back is written exactly like the received text
    public static function validDate(mixed $text): ?DateTimeImmutable
    {
        if (! is_string($text) || ! preg_match('/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/', $text)) {
            return null;
        }
        // "!Y-m-d": the exclamation mark sets the time to midnight
        $date = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('!Y-m-d', $text);
        return $date !== false && $date->format('Y-m-d') === $text ? $date : null;
    }

    public static function iso(DateTimeImmutable $day): string
    {
        return $day->format('Y-m-d');
    }

    // "mercredi 23 septembre 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026", depending on the language
    // of the request (see example 16). The ICU pattern: EEEE the day of the week in
    // full, d the day, MMMM the month in full, y the year
    public function formatDay(DateTimeImmutable $day): string
    {
        $language = $this->requests->getCurrentRequest()?->getLocale() ?? 'en';
        return (new IntlDateFormatter($language, IntlDateFormatter::NONE, IntlDateFormatter::NONE,
            pattern: 'EEEE d MMMM y'))->format($day);
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- input

    // "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", "+2", null -> null
    public static function positiveInteger(mixed $value): ?int
    {
        if (! is_string($value) || ! preg_match('/^\d{1,9}$/', $value)) {
            return null;
        }
        $n = (int) $value;
        return $n > 0 ? $n : null;
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- user

    // the logged-in user. The protected actions are only called if they exist;
    // as a precaution, their absence is treated as an expired session
    public function user(): ConnectedUser
    {
        $user = $this->security->getUser();
        return $user instanceof ConnectedUser ? $user : throw new InvalidSession();
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // The patient (Client entity) that matches the logged-in user.
    //
    // The JWT token only contains the id of the ACCOUNT (users.id). For a USER role, we
    // find the matching client thanks to the clients.user column.
    //
    // If there is none, it means the account has been deleted since the login
    // while its token is still valid: we treat it as an expired
    // session (see InvalidSession).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function connectedPatient(): Client
    {
        return $this->application->getClientByUserId($this->user()->userId)
            ?? throw new InvalidSession();
    }
}

Some utility functions. The static methods are called without an object ([Utils::iso($day)]); the others require services: the class is therefore also a service, which the controllers receive via their constructor.

  • Lines 38–46: the date of a parameter [yyyy-mm-dd] or [null]. Two checks: the format (a regular expression), then the existence of the date. [createFromFormat] is tolerant: February 30 becomes March 2. We then re-read the resulting date and verify that it is written exactly as the received text. The [!] in the format sets the time to midnight (without it, the time would be the current time). [mixed]: any type;
  • lines 56–61: “Saturday 26 September 2026” or “samedi 26 septembre 2026,” depending on the language of the request. [IntlDateFormatter] (example 16), with a pattern rather than a style: the codes are those from the ICU library, [EEEE] for the day of the week spelled out, [d] for the day, [MMMM] for the month spelled out, and [y] for the year. The parameter [pattern] is passed by name: the parameters that precede it in the signature—and for which no value is provided—retain their default values;
  • lines 66–73: A request parameter can be a string, such as [null], or even an array ([?doctorId[]=1], example 10). Only digits are accepted (up to nine: to avoid exceeding capacity), and the number must be strictly positive;
  • lines 79–83: the logged-in user, determined by the authenticator, which is returned by the [Security] service of [Symfony]. Protected actions are called only for an authenticated user, but the user’s absence is still handled as an expired session. [throw] is an expression ([PHP] 8): it can appear in the operator [? :];
  • lines 95–99: the patient (the [Client]) of the logged-in user. The token contains only the account ID; the client is identified by the [clients.user] column. If it does not exist, the account has been deleted since the user logged in: [InvalidSession].

docs.title: 11.15.5. src/Twig/ViewsExtension.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Twig/ViewsExtension.php: a Twig extension (see example 16), which adds
// to the views the functions that ALL the pages need:
//   - user()   : the logged-in user (or null), for the navigation bar;
//   - titles() : the possible titles of a person (Mr, Mme, Melle).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Twig;

use App\Form\PersonFieldsType;
use App\Security\AuthService;
use App\Security\ConnectedUser;
use Symfony\Bundle\SecurityBundle\Security;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;
use Twig\Extension\AbstractExtension;
use Twig\TwigFunction;

class ViewsExtension extends AbstractExtension
{
    public function __construct(
        private Security $security,
        private RequestStack $requests,
        private AuthService $auth,
    ) {
    }

    public function getFunctions(): array
    {
        return [
            new TwigFunction('user', $this->user(...)),
            new TwigFunction('titles', fn () => PersonFieldsType::TITLES),
        ];
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the user established by the firewall. A 404 or 405 error page is
    // built BEFORE the firewall (routing, which fails, comes before it, see
    // example 24): the user is then read directly from the token, so that
    // the navigation bar of the error page is complete
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function user(): ?ConnectedUser
    {
        $user = $this->security->getUser();
        if ($user instanceof ConnectedUser) {
            return $user;
        }
        $token = $this->requests->getMainRequest()?->cookies->getString(AuthService::COOKIE);
        return $token ? $this->auth->currentUser($token) : null;
    }
}

An extension of [Twig] (Example 16), which adds two functions to the views that all pages need:

  • [user()]: the logged-in user, or [null], for the navigation bar. Usually, this is the one from the [Security] service (line 44). However, a 404 or 405 error page is generated before the firewall has examined the request: the routing, which fails, takes precedence over it (Example 24). The user is then retrieved directly from the token (lines 48–49) so that the navigation bar on the error page is complete. [getMainRequest] makes the main request; the operator [?->] returns [null] without calling the method if the object is [null];
  • [titles()]: the possible titles for a person ([Mr], [Mme], [Melle]), a constant in the person form class (see below).

[$this->user(...)] (line 31) is the syntax for first-class functions ([PHP] 8.1): it creates a function that calls the [user] method of that object. The extension is automatically declared as [Twig], just like in Example 16: the container recognizes a class that inherits from [AbstractExtension].

docs.title: 11.16. Dictionaries
docs.text:
The interface texts are the same as those in other versions of the application, which stored them in nested JSON files:

{
  "LOGIN": {
    "TITLE": "Login",
    "USERNAME": "Login"
  }
}

The [Flask] version “flattened” them at startup: [LOGIN.TITLE] referred to the text [Login]. The YAML dictionaries from [Symfony] do the same (example 22): nested keys are separated by periods. We therefore simply converted the JSON files to YAML, and replaced the [{{name}}] parameters in the other versions with those of the ICU syntax, [{name}] (the [+intl-icu] suffix in the filenames, example 22):

APP:
    TITLE: 'RdvMedecins'
    LOGOUT: 'Log out'
DOCTORS:
    ADDED: 'Doctor {name} has been added (login: {login}).'
ERRORS:
    TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS: 'Too many failed attempts. Try again in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.'

The files [translations/messages+intl-icu.fr.yaml] and [messages+intl-icu.en.yaml] are not reproduced here. A key is represented by [{{ 'APP.LOGOUT'|trans }}] in a view, and a parameterized text by [{{ 'DOCTORS.ADDED'|trans({name: ..., login: ...}) }}]. A key missing from the dictionary is displayed as-is, which immediately flags an omission (and the command [php bin/console debug:translation fr] lists the keys used by the views that are missing from the dictionary). ICU enables something that previous versions could not do: the plural (“1 minute,” “15 minutes”), using the format [plural] (example 22). A text entry has been added: [ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED], the message on page 419, which is not present in other versions.

Form error messages are also keys in these dictionaries ([ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED]...): the validation component translates them into the [messages] domain, using the line [translation_domain: messages] from [framework.yaml]. Their parameters correspond to the constraints: [{limit}], for the minimum password length.

docs.title: 11.17. Forms
docs.text: "Person" forms are forms from the Form component (examples 18 and 19): a type class describes the fields and their constraints; the action creates the form ([createForm]), passes the request to it ([handleRequest]), and then checks whether it has been submitted and is valid ([isSubmitted], [isValid]). An invalid form is redisplayed, showing the user’s input and error messages below the fields (excluding passwords: a [PasswordType] field is never redisplayed). The anti-CSRF token for each form is verified by the component itself.

docs.title: 11.17.1. src/Form/PersonFieldsType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Form/PersonFieldsType.php: the fields of the "person" forms and their
// constraints (see examples 18 and 19). Three forms share the same identity
// fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//   PersonFieldsType            title, first name, last name
//    ├─ PersonType              + OPTIONAL login / password, version
//    │                            (the ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor / client)
//    ├─ RegistrationType        + REQUIRED login / password / confirmation
//    │                            (a patient creates their account)
//    └─ MyAccountType           + login, optional new password, REQUIRED
//                                 CURRENT password, version
//                                 (a patient modifies their account)
//
// The child classes INHERIT from this one (in the PHP sense): their buildForm first
// calls that of the parent, then adds its fields.
//
// The forms have no data class (data_class, see example 19): the
// validated input is an associative array, which the data() method turns into
// PersonData for the business layer.
//
// The labels, the help texts and the error messages are KEYS of the
// dictionaries: the Form component translates the labels and the help texts, the
// Validator component the messages (see config/packages/framework.yaml).
// Sequentially: the constraints are checked in order, and the check
// stops at the first one that is not satisfied - only one message per field.
// The maximum lengths are those of the SQL columns.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Form;

use App\Business\PersonData;
use Symfony\Component\Form\AbstractType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\CallbackTransformer;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\ChoiceType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\TextType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\OptionsResolver\OptionsResolver;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

abstract class PersonFieldsType extends AbstractType
{
    public const TITLES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

    // login: lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore - 30 characters at most
    public const LOGIN_FORMAT = '/^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/';

    // minimum length of a password CHOSEN by a patient
    public const PASSWORD_MIN = 6;

    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        $builder
            // array_combine: ['Mr' => 'Mr', ...], the label and the value of each
            // option; choice_translation_domain false: the titles are not translated
            ->add('title', ChoiceType::class, [
                'label' => 'PERSONS.TITLE_LABEL',
                'choices' => array_combine(self::TITLES, self::TITLES),
                'choice_translation_domain' => false,
                'invalid_message' => 'ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE',
                'constraints' => [new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE')],
            ])
            ->add('first_name', TextType::class, [
                'label' => 'PERSONS.FIRSTNAME_LABEL',
                'attr' => ['maxlength' => 20],
                'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                    new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED'),
                    new Assert\Length(max: 20, maxMessage: 'ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG'),
                ])],
            ])
            ->add('last_name', TextType::class, [
                'label' => 'PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL',
                'attr' => ['maxlength' => 20],
                'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                    new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED'),
                    new Assert\Length(max: 20, maxMessage: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG'),
                ])],
            ]);
    }

    // the common options: an invalid form sent back as is to the browser,
    // without validation by the browser itself (see example 19: it is the SERVER
    // that is authoritative); the message of a wrong anti-CSRF token
    public function configureOptions(OptionsResolver $resolver): void
    {
        $resolver->setDefaults([
            'attr' => ['novalidate' => 'novalidate'],
            'csrf_message' => 'ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED',
        ]);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the login field, common to the child forms. A login is always in
    // lower case: a TRANSFORMER (CallbackTransformer) converts the input BEFORE
    // its validation. Its first function turns the value of the form into
    // displayed text (here, nothing to do), the second one the input into the value of the form
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    protected static function addLogin(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        $builder->add('login', TextType::class, ['label' => 'PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL', 'required' => false,
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 30, 'autocomplete' => 'off'], ...$options]);
        $builder->get('login')->addModelTransformer(new CallbackTransformer(
            fn (?string $login) => $login,
            fn (?string $login) => $login === null ? null : mb_strtolower($login)));
    }

    // the validated input -> the data expected by the business layer. The empty
    // fields are null (the Form component converts them so)
    public static function data(array $input): PersonData
    {
        $password = $input['password'] ?? null;
        return new PersonData($input['title'], $input['last_name'], $input['first_name'],
            $input['login'] ?? null, $password === '' ? null : $password,
            isset($input['version']) && ctype_digit((string) $input['version']) ? (int) $input['version'] : null);
    }
}

Three forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name): the administrator form (for a doctor or a client), the patient account creation form, and “Manage My Account.” Their common parent class is abstract; each of its child classes extends these fields. None of these forms has a data class (the [data_class] option from Example 19): their data consists of an associative array, with one element per field.

  • lines 44–50: the input rules, in the form of constants, which are also read by the views (the list of titles, by function [titles()] from extension [Twig]);
  • lines 57–63: the title, a list ([ChoiceType], Example 18). [array_combine] generates the array [['Mr' => 'Mr', ...]]: the label for each option and its value. [choice_translation_domain: false]: The titles are not translation keys. [invalid_message]: The message for a value that is not part of the list (a manually constructed query);
  • Lines 64–79: first name and last name. The constraint [Sequentially] (example 09) checks its constraints in order and stops at the first one that is not met: only one message per field. [Length(max: 20)]: 20 characters maximum; the column length is SQL; the attribute HTML [maxlength] prevents more characters from being entered. Spaces at the beginning and end of an entry are removed by the Form component itself (the [trim] option for a text field is set to [true]), and an empty entry becomes [null]; a field with the option [PasswordType], on the other hand, is not cleaned: spaces can be part of a password;
  • Lines 85–91: common options. [novalidate] disables browser validations ([required], [maxlength]...) when the form is submitted: the server performs the validation, and its result is final (example 19). [csrf_message]: the message for a invalid anti-CSRF token, the one from the 419 page;
  • lines 99–106: the login, common to all three girls, to which each adds her own options (the operator [...] adds elements from one array to another; a key present in both takes on the last value). A login is always in lowercase: a transformer converts the input before it is validated. A model transformer ([addModelTransformer]) has two functions: the first transforms the form data into a displayed value (in this case, no action is required), and the second transforms the entered value into form data. [CallbackTransformer] creates a transformer based on these two functions;
  • Lines 110–116: The validated input is converted to [PersonData] for the business layer: the business layer is not aware of the forms. An empty password is [null] (unchanged, or the default value); the version (the hidden field of the optimistic lock, e.g., 28) is an integer, or [null].

docs.title: 11.17.2. src/Form/PersonType.php, RegistrationType.php, MyAccountType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Form/PersonType.php: the form of a doctor or of a client (ADMIN):
// OPTIONAL login and password (see src/Business/PersonData.php).

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\HiddenType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\OptionsResolver\OptionsResolver;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class PersonType extends PersonFieldsType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        parent::buildForm($builder, $options);
        $creation = $options['creation'];
        // an empty field is accepted: the constraints only apply to an entered value
        self::addLogin($builder, [
            'help' => $creation ? 'PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_CREATE' : 'PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_EDIT',
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Regex(self::LOGIN_FORMAT, message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN')],
        ]);
        $builder->add('password', PasswordType::class, [
            'label' => 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL',
            'required' => false,
            'help' => $creation ? 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_CREATE' : 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT',
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 72, 'autocomplete' => 'new-password'],
            // 72 characters at most: beyond that, bcrypt ignores the rest
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Length(max: 72, maxMessage: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG')],
        ]);
        // modification: the version of the displayed record, in a hidden field (the
        // optimistic lock)
        if (! $creation) {
            $builder->add('version', HiddenType::class);
        }
    }

    // an option of our own (see example 28): creation form, or modification form
    public function configureOptions(OptionsResolver $resolver): void
    {
        parent::configureOptions($resolver);
        $resolver->setDefaults(['creation' => true]);
    }
}

The administrator form. [parent::buildForm] (line 17) adds the fields from the parent class; next come the username and password, which are optional: a constraint applies only to a value that is entered (except for [NotBlank]), so an empty field is accepted. [Regex] validates the login format; [Length(max: 72)] limits the password length: [bcrypt] considers only the first 72 bytes (Example 25). The option [creation] (lines 40–44), an option we devised, declared with its default value (example 28), distinguishes between creation and modification: the tooltips differ (“Optional: defaults to the last name in lower case,” “Leave empty to keep it unchanged”), and only the modification has the hidden version field.

<?php
// src/Form/RegistrationType.php: "Create a patient account": REQUIRED login, password and
// confirmation.

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\RepeatedType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class RegistrationType extends PersonFieldsType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        parent::buildForm($builder, $options);
        self::addLogin($builder, [
            'required' => true,
            'help' => 'REGISTRATION.LOGIN_HELP',
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 30, 'autocomplete' => 'username'],
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED'),
                new Assert\Regex(self::LOGIN_FORMAT, message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN'),
            ])],
        ]);
        $builder->add('password', RepeatedType::class, self::repeatedPassword(true));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the password and its confirmation: a REPEATED field (see example 19), whose
    // two inputs must be identical (otherwise: invalid_message). Common to
    // the registration (required) and to the patient's account (optional).
    // {limit}: in the PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT message, the minimum length;
    // help_translation_parameters: the parameters of the help text
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static function repeatedPassword(bool $required): array
    {
        $length = new Assert\Length(min: self::PASSWORD_MIN, max: 72,
            minMessage: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT', maxMessage: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG');
        return [
            'type' => PasswordType::class,
            'required' => $required,
            'invalid_message' => 'ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER',
            'first_options' => [
                'label' => $required ? 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL' : 'MY_ACCOUNT.NEW_PASSWORD_LABEL',
                'help' => $required ? 'REGISTRATION.PASSWORD_HELP' : 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT',
                'help_translation_parameters' => ['min' => self::PASSWORD_MIN],
            ],
            'second_options' => ['label' => 'ACCOUNT.CONFIRMATION_LABEL'],
            'options' => ['attr' => ['maxlength' => 72, 'autocomplete' => 'new-password']],
            'constraints' => $required
                ? [new Assert\Sequentially([new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED'), $length])]
                : [$length],
        ];
    }
}

Creating a patient account: login and password are required, and the password must be confirmed. The password is a repeated field ([RepeatedType], example 19): two [PasswordType] fields, whose entries must be identical (otherwise, the message [invalid_message] is displayed below the first one). Its options are generated by a static method, shared with “Manage My Account” (lines 36–55):

  • [first_options] and [second_options]: the options for each of the two fields; [options]: the options they have in common;
  • [help_translation_parameters]: the parameters for the help text, “At least {min} characters.”;
  • the minimum length is required only for the password chosen by a patient (6 characters). The message [ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT] contains [{limit}], the parameter that the constraint [Length] provides to its message;
  • [autocomplete="new-password"]: The browser offers to generate a password instead of filling in the field with the saved password.
<?php
// src/Form/MyAccountType.php: "Manage my account" (a patient): required login,
// optional new password, REQUIRED current password.

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\HiddenType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\RepeatedType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class MyAccountType extends PersonFieldsType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        parent::buildForm($builder, $options);
        self::addLogin($builder, [
            'required' => true,
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 30, 'autocomplete' => 'username'],
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED'),
                new Assert\Regex(self::LOGIN_FORMAT, message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN'),
            ])],
        ]);
        // optional: empty = password unchanged
        $builder->add('password', RepeatedType::class, RegistrationType::repeatedPassword(false));
        // the CURRENT password, required for any modification of the account; mapped
        // false: it is not part of the data of the form, it is read separately
        $builder->add('current_password', PasswordType::class, [
            'label' => 'MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL',
            'help' => 'MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_HELP',
            'mapped' => false,
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 72, 'autocomplete' => 'current-password'],
            'constraints' => [new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED')],
        ]);
        $builder->add('version', HiddenType::class);
    }
}

“Manage My Account”: the new password is optional (empty: unchanged), the current password is required. [mapped: false] (line 33): the current password is not part of the form data ([getData()] does not contain it); the action reads it separately, via [$form->get('current_password')->getData()]. It is not validated here, but by the action: an incorrect password must be counted by the attempt limiter as a failed login. ([Symfony] has a constraint, [UserPassword], which compares the entered password to the logged-in user’s password; this constraint is not applicable here: our logged-in user, [ConnectedUser], does not contain the hash of their password.)

docs.title: 11.18. View Templates
docs.text:
The [src/Views] folder contains the view templates: objects created by an action, which the view simply reads. The rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. Actions prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; the views place this data into the HTML. All these classes are of type [readonly] and have only properties, which are initialized by their constructor. The folder is excluded from the services ([config/services.yaml]): these are data, not services.

<?php
// src/Views/OptionView.php: an option of a drop-down list (doctor, patient).
//
// The src/Views folder contains the "view models": objects
// built in one go by an action, which the view merely reads. Rule
// followed by all the pages: no logic in the views. The actions
// prepare data ALREADY formatted ("Mme Marie PELISSIER",
// "8:00 - 8:20", selected = true...) and already filtered according to the role of
// the user; the views merely place them in the HTML.

namespace App\Views;

readonly class OptionView
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $id,
        public string $label,
        public bool $selected,
    ) {
    }
}

An option in a drop-down list: the ID, the label, and whether the option is selected?

<?php
// src/Views/ScheduleRow.php: a row of the displayed schedule (a slot).

namespace App\Views;

readonly class ScheduleRow
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $slotId,
        public string $time,         // "8:00 - 8:20"
        public bool $free,
        // displayed name for a taken slot; null = "Booked"
        public ?string $patient,
        public bool $mine,           // the appointment of the logged-in patient
        public bool $bookable,       // display the "Book" button?
        public string $bookUrl,
        // set only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
        public ?int $appointmentId,
    ) {
    }
}

A calendar entry: a time slot, and what the logged-in user is authorized to view and do with it. [patient] is populated only if the user has permission to see the patient’s name; [bookable] indicates whether to display the “Book” button; [appointmentId] indicates whether to display the “Cancel” button.

<?php
// src/Views/ScheduleView.php: the displayed schedule: the doctor, the day, the rows.

namespace App\Views;

readonly class ScheduleView
{
    /** @param list<ScheduleRow> $rows */
    public function __construct(
        public string $doctor,       // "Mme Marie PELISSIER"
        public string $day,          // "Wednesday 23 September 2026"
        public array $rows,
    ) {
    }
}

<?php
// src/Views/BookingView.php: the booking dialog of a slot.

namespace App\Views;

readonly class BookingView
{
    /** @param list<OptionView> $clients */
    public function __construct(
        public int $slotId,
        public string $time,
        // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the patients to choose from
        public array $clients,
        // USER: the patient is themselves
        public ?string $patient,
    ) {
    }
}

The displayed calendar and the booking window: for the administrator and doctors, the list of patients to choose from; for a patient, their own name. The comment [/** @param list<ScheduleRow> $rows */] specifies, for editors and analysis tools, the contents of the table: [PHP] can only declare the type [array].

<?php
// src/Views/PersonKeys.php: the translation keys specific to each type of
// person (doctors or clients), for the common views persons/list and
// persons/form.

namespace App\Views;

readonly class PersonKeys
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $title,                 // "Doctors"
        public string $add,                   // "Add a doctor"
        public string $edit,                  // "Edit a doctor"
        public string $empty,                 // "No doctors."
        public string $confirmDelete,         // "Delete this doctor... ?"
        public string $added,                 // "Doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
        public string $edited,
        public string $deleted,
    ) {
    }

    // the eight keys of a section of the dictionary ("DOCTORS", "CLIENTS")
    public static function of(string $section): self
    {
        return new self("$section.TITLE", "$section.ADD", "$section.EDIT", "$section.EMPTY",
            "$section.DELETE_CONFIRM", "$section.ADDED", "$section.UPDATED", "$section.DELETED");
    }
}

Translation keys specific to doctors or clients, for the two views they have in common. The static method [of] (lines 23–27) generates the eight keys for a section of the dictionaries: [PersonKeys::of('DOCTORS')] yields [DOCTORS.TITLE], [DOCTORS.ADD]... [new self(...)] creates an object of the class itself.

<?php
// src/Views/AppointmentView.php: an upcoming appointment, in the patient's area.

namespace App\Views;

readonly class AppointmentView
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $id,
        public string $day,          // "Wednesday 23 September 2026"
        public string $time,         // "8:00 - 8:20"
        public string $doctor,       // "Mme Marie PELISSIER"
        public string $scheduleUrl,  // the doctor's schedule on that day
    ) {
    }
}

An upcoming appointment in the patient area.

docs.title: 11.19. The web layer: routes and controllers
11.19.1. Routes
docs.text:
Routes are described by the [#[Route]] attributes of controllers (Example 02), which are loaded by the [config/routes.yaml] file. The [debug:router] command lists them all, along with their names, methods, and paths:

$ php bin/console debug:router
 --------------------- ---------- ----------------------
  Name                  Method     Path
 --------------------- ---------- ----------------------
  home                  GET        /
  login                 GET        /login
  login_submit          POST       /login
  logout                POST       /logout
  clients_list          GET        /clients
  clients_add           GET|POST   /clients/add
  clients_edit          GET|POST   /clients/{id}/edit
  clients_delete        POST       /clients/{id}/delete
  doctors_list          GET        /doctors
  doctors_add           GET|POST   /doctors/add
  doctors_edit          GET|POST   /doctors/{id}/edit
  doctors_delete        POST       /doctors/{id}/delete
  language              GET        /language/{code}
  area                  GET        /my-area
  area_cancel           POST       /my-area/cancel
  account               GET|POST   /my-account
  account_delete        POST       /my-account/delete
  registration_access   POST       /register/access
  registration          GET|POST   /register
  schedule              GET        /schedule
  schedule_book         POST       /schedule/book
  schedule_cancel       POST       /schedule/cancel
 --------------------- ---------- ----------------------

The URL files correspond to other versions of the application: modifying and deleting a doctor are POST requests ([/doctors/{id}/edit], [/doctors/{id}/delete]), not PUT and DELETE as in Example 28. The code always generates the URL based on the route names ([redirectToRoute('login')], [path('schedule')] in the views, Example 04): changing a URL requires modifying only its [#[Route]] attribute.

Access rules are not in the controllers, but in the [access_control] rules of [config/packages/security.yaml], as shown above: one rule per URL prefix ([^/(doctors|clients)] for the administrator, [^/my-] for patients...), and a final rule that requires an authenticated user for all other URL. The application’s URL routes were chosen for this purpose: all pages within the same role begin the same way. A URL route that does not match any route returns a 404 page, even to an anonymous visitor; a request for GET directed at a URL that exists only as POST ([/logout]) results in a 405 page, presented as a "page not found" (handler [ErrorPage]).

docs.title: 11.19.2. src/Controller/LanguageController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/LanguageController.php: GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two
// FR / EN buttons of the navigation bar. Public route: one must be able to
// change the language before logging in.
//
// The choice is remembered in a cookie: on each following request, the listener
// SetLanguage reads it again and sets the language of the request. Then we go back to the
// page we came from (see example 22).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\EventListener\SetLanguage;
use App\Web\BaseController;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Cookie;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class LanguageController extends BaseController
{
    public function __construct(#[Autowire(env: 'bool:COOKIE_SECURE')] private bool $cookieSecure)
    {
    }

    // {code} is limited to the supported languages (requirements): /language/de gives a 404 page
    #[Route('/language/{code}', name: 'language', requirements: ['code' => 'fr|en'], methods: ['GET'])]
    public function change(Request $request, string $code): Response
    {
        $response = $this->redirect($this->originPage($request));
        $response->headers->setCookie(Cookie::create(SetLanguage::COOKIE, $code)
            ->withExpires(new \DateTimeImmutable('+1 year'))
            ->withSecure($this->cookieSecure)
            ->withHttpOnly(true)
            ->withSameSite(Cookie::SAMESITE_LAX));
        return $response;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the previous page, according to the HTTP "Referer" header sent by the browser.
    // Only its path is kept (/schedule?...): redirecting to a complete
    // address provided by the request would allow sending the user to
    // another site (so-called "open redirect" flaw).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function originPage(Request $request): string
    {
        $referer = $request->headers->get('Referer');
        $url = $referer ? parse_url($referer) : false;
        $path = $url['path'] ?? '';
        // "//site.com/..." would be understood by the browser as an address on
        // ANOTHER site: refused too
        if (! isset($url['scheme']) || ! str_starts_with($path, '/') || str_starts_with($path, '//')
            || str_starts_with($path, '/language/')) {
            return '/';
        }
        return isset($url['query']) ? "$path?{$url['query']}" : $path;
    }
}

The FR / EN buttons on the navigation bar: the language selection is stored in a cookie for one year (example 22), then the browser returns to the page it came from. The cookie is [HttpOnly]: the [JavaScript] on the page does not need to read it. It is unsigned: the listener [SetLanguage] verifies its value, and an unknown value results in English (see the chapter on ranges).

  • Line 29: [requirements: ['code' => 'fr|en']] accepts only these two values for the parameter [{code}]: [/language/de] does not correspond to any route (404 page);
  • Lines 47–59: The previous page is specified by the header HTTP ***[Referer], which the browser sends with the request. This data is provided by the client and is therefore suspect: redirecting to a full URL from the request would allow an attacker to send the user to their own site via a link to [/language/fr] that includes a fake ***[Referer] (the so-called “open redirect” vulnerability). Therefore, we retain only the path and parameters ([/schedule?doctorId=1&...]), extracted by the function [parse_url] from [PHP], which splits a URL into its parts ([scheme], [host], [path], [query]...). A path starting with [//] is also rejected: a browser interprets [//site.com/page] as an address on another site. Finally, we cannot return to [/language/...]: a loop.

docs.title: 11.19.3. src/Controller/ScheduleController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/ScheduleController.php: the schedule page: choice of a doctor and
// of a day, schedule of that doctor on that day, booking and cancellation of
// appointments.
//
//   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23               the page
//   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7        the same page, with the
//                                                          booking dialog
//                                                          of slot 7 open
//   POST /schedule/book                                    creates an appointment
//   POST /schedule/cancel                                  cancels an appointment
//
// The whole page is described by its URL: it can be reloaded, bookmarked,
// the browser's "Back" button can be used - without a single line of
// JavaScript.
//
// What each one sees and can do:
//
//   | role          | taken slot displayed              | Book               | Cancel  |
//   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
//   | ADMIN, DOCTOR | name of the patient               | for a patient      | yes     |
//   |               |                                   | chosen in a list   |         |
//   | USER (patient)| "Booked", or THEIR name if it is  | for themselves, if | no (*)  |
//   |               | their own appointment             | they have no       |         |
//   |               |                                   | upcoming one       |         |
//
//   (*) the patient cancels their appointment from their "My area" page.
//
// CONFIDENTIALITY: for a patient, the name of the OTHER patients is not
// simply hidden by the view - it is never passed to the view. The HTML sent
// to the browser therefore does not contain it, not even hidden (a simple "View page
// source" would otherwise reveal it).
//
// No booking in the past: the "Book" button only appears for
// today and the following days (and the business layer would refuse it
// anyway).
//
// Security: all the /schedule URLs require an authenticated user, and
// /schedule/cancel the ADMIN or DOCTOR role (see config/packages/security.yaml).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Domain\DoctorDaySchedule;
use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Person;
use App\Entity\Role;
use App\Business\Dates;
use App\Business\BusinessException;
use App\Views\ScheduleView;
use App\Views\ScheduleRow;
use App\Views\OptionView;
use App\Views\BookingView;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use App\Web\BaseController;
use App\Web\Flash;
use App\Web\Message;
use App\Web\Utils;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\BadRequestHttpException;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route('/schedule')]
class ScheduleController extends BaseController
{
    public function __construct(
        private ApplicationModel $application,
        private Utils $utils,
        private Flash $flash,
    ) {
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /schedule
    // The parameters of the URL are read raw ($request->query), to distinguish an
    // ABSENT parameter (null) from an EMPTY parameter (?doctorId=).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('', name: 'schedule', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function show(Request $request): Response
    {
        $error = null;
        $user = $this->utils->user();
        $rights = $this->rights();

        // the day: that of the URL if it is valid, otherwise today
        $day = Dates::today();
        $rawDay = $request->query->get('day');
        if ($rawDay !== null) {
            $requestedDay = Utils::validDate($rawDay);
            if ($requestedDay !== null) {
                $day = $requestedDay;
            } else {
                $error = 'ERRORS.INVALID_DATE';
            }
        }
        $bookableDay = $day >= Dates::today();

        // the doctor: that of the URL; failing that, for a logged-in doctor, themselves
        $rawDoctorId = $request->query->get('doctorId');
        $doctorId = Utils::positiveInteger($rawDoctorId);
        if ($rawDoctorId === null && $user->role === Role::DOCTOR) {
            $doctorId = $this->application->getDoctorByUserId($user->userId)?->getId();
        }

        // the drop-down list of the doctors
        $doctors = array_map(fn (Person $d) => self::option($d, $d->getId() === $doctorId),
            $this->application->getAllDoctors());

        // the schedule, if a doctor is chosen (and the date valid)
        $schedule = null;
        if ($doctorId !== null && $error === null) {
            $doctorSchedule = $this->application->getDoctorDaySchedule($doctorId, $day);
            if ($doctorSchedule === null) {
                $error = 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND';
            } else {
                $schedule = $this->scheduleView($doctorSchedule, $rights, $bookableDay);
            }
        }

        // the booking dialog: only if the requested slot can be booked
        // by this user. array_find: the first element that satisfies the
        // condition (null if there is none)
        $booking = null;
        $slotId = Utils::positiveInteger($request->query->get('book'));
        if ($schedule !== null && $slotId !== null) {
            $row = array_find($schedule->rows,
                fn (ScheduleRow $r) => $r->slotId === $slotId && $r->bookable);
            if ($row !== null) {
                $booking = new BookingView(
                    $row->slotId,
                    $row->time,
                    $rights['manager']
                        ? array_map(fn (Client $c) => self::option($c, false), $this->application->getAllClients())
                        : [],
                    $rights['patient']?->label());
            }
        }

        return $this->render('schedule.html.twig', [
            'pageTitle' => 'SCHEDULE.PAGE_TITLE',
            'error' => $error ? new Message($error) : null,
            'doctors' => $doctors,
            'doctorId' => $doctorId,
            'day' => Utils::iso($day),
            'schedule' => $schedule,
            'booking' => $booking,
            // the displayed schedule, without booking dialog
            'backUrl' => $doctorId !== null ? $this->scheduleUrl($doctorId, $day) : $this->generateUrl('schedule'),
            'info' => $this->patientInfo($rights, $schedule),
        ]);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /schedule/book   fields: doctorId, day, slotId, clientId
    //
    // For a patient (USER), the clientId field is IGNORED: they always book
    // for themselves. Trusting a field sent by the browser
    // would allow a cunning patient to book in the name of another one.
    //
    // "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern: whatever the result, no page is built
    // here - a flash message is left and we redirect to the schedule
    // (see example 20).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/book', name: 'schedule_book', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function book(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        [$doctorId, $day] = $this->requestedSchedule($request);
        $slotId = Utils::positiveInteger($request->request->get('slotId'));
        if ($doctorId === null || $slotId === null) {
            // -> "invalid request" page (see src/EventListener/ErrorPage.php)
            throw new BadRequestHttpException('invalid schedule or slot');
        }
        $user = $this->utils->user();

        if ($user->isPatient()) {
            $client = $this->utils->connectedPatient();
        } else {
            $clientId = Utils::positiveInteger($request->request->get('clientId'));
            if ($clientId === null) {
                // no patient chosen: the booking dialog is opened again
                $this->flash->error('ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT');
                return $this->redirect($this->scheduleUrl($doctorId, $day, $slotId));
            }
            $client = $this->application->getClientById($clientId);
        }

        $slot = $this->application->getSlotById($slotId);
        if ($client === null) {
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND');
        } elseif ($slot === null || $slot->getDoctor()->getId() !== $doctorId) {
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND');
        } else {
            try {
                // the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
                // patient, free slot) are checked by the business layer
                $this->application->addAppointment($day, $slot, $client);
                $this->flash->success('SCHEDULE.BOOKED');
            } catch (BusinessException $e) {
                // same rule, but a message in the 2nd person when it is the
                // patient themselves who books ("You already have..." rather than
                // "This patient..."). The other exceptions (real anomalies) are not
                // caught: 500 page.
                if ($e->key === 'ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT' && $user->isPatient()) {
                    $this->flash->error('SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO');
                } else {
                    $this->flash->error($e->key, $e->params);
                }
            }
        }
        return $this->redirect($this->scheduleUrl($doctorId, $day));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /schedule/cancel   fields: appointmentId, doctorId, day
    // (a patient cancels THEIR appointment from "My area", not from here)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/cancel', name: 'schedule_cancel', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function cancel(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        [$doctorId, $day] = $this->requestedSchedule($request);
        $appointmentId = Utils::positiveInteger($request->request->get('appointmentId'));
        if ($doctorId === null || $appointmentId === null) {
            throw new BadRequestHttpException('invalid schedule or appointment');
        }
        $appointment = $this->application->getAppointmentById($appointmentId);
        if ($appointment === null) {
            // already cancelled (by someone else, or double click)
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND');
        } else {
            $this->application->deleteAppointment($appointment);
            $this->flash->success('SCHEDULE.CANCELLED');
        }
        return $this->redirect($this->scheduleUrl($doctorId, $day));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // who is logged in, and what are they allowed to do on this page?
    //   manager: ADMIN or DOCTOR;
    //   patient: the logged-in client (USER role), otherwise null;
