    //   patientCanBook: a USER without an upcoming appointment.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function rights(): array
    {
        if (! $this->utils->user()->isPatient()) {
            return ['manager' => true, 'patient' => null, 'patientCanBook' => false];
        }
        $patient = $this->utils->connectedPatient();
        $upcoming = $this->application->getClientUpcomingAppointments($patient->getId());
        return ['manager' => false, 'patient' => $patient, 'patientCanBook' => $upcoming === []];
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the doctor's schedule, formatted for the view - and filtered according to the rights
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function scheduleView(DoctorDaySchedule $doctorSchedule, array $rights, bool $bookableDay): ScheduleView
    {
        $doctorId = $doctorSchedule->doctor->getId();
        $day = $doctorSchedule->day;
        $rows = [];
        foreach ($doctorSchedule->doctorDaySlots as $dds) {
            $slot = $dds->slot;
            $appointment = $dds->appointment;
            $free = $appointment === null;
            // the appointment of the logged-in patient?
            $mine = $appointment !== null && $rights['patient'] !== null
                && $appointment->getClient()->getId() === $rights['patient']->getId();
            $rows[] = new ScheduleRow(
                slotId: $slot->getId(),
                time: $slot->time(),
                free: $free,
                // THE confidentiality point: a patient only receives the name of
                // THEIR appointment; for the others, null (the view displays "Booked")
                patient: $appointment !== null && ($rights['manager'] || $mine) ? $appointment->getClient()->label() : null,
                mine: $mine,
                bookable: $free && $bookableDay && ($rights['manager'] || $rights['patientCanBook']),
                bookUrl: $this->scheduleUrl($doctorId, $day, $slot->getId()),
                appointmentId: $appointment !== null && $rights['manager'] ? $appointment->getId() : null);
        }
        return new ScheduleView($doctorSchedule->doctor->label(), $this->utils->formatDay($day), $rows);
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- utility functions

    // the hidden fields doctorId / day of the POST forms; [null, null] if they
    // are invalid
    private function requestedSchedule(Request $request): array
    {
        $doctorId = Utils::positiveInteger($request->request->get('doctorId'));
        $day = Utils::validDate($request->request->get('day'));
        return $doctorId === null || $day === null ? [null, null] : [$doctorId, $day];
    }

    // /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23[&book=7]: generateUrl appends to the end
    // of the URL the parameters that are not parameters of the path (see example 16)
    private function scheduleUrl(int $doctorId, DateTimeImmutable $day, ?int $book = null): string
    {
        $params = ['doctorId' => $doctorId, 'day' => Utils::iso($day)];
        if ($book !== null) {
            $params['book'] = $book;
        }
        return $this->generateUrl('schedule', $params);
    }

    private static function option(Person $p, bool $selected): OptionView
    {
        return new OptionView($p->getId(), $p->label(), $selected);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the information message of a patient who already has an upcoming appointment
    // (why there is no "Book" button), or null. Useless if THEIR
    // appointment appears in the displayed schedule (in blue): that is the case right
    // after they have just booked it, when the message would be out of place.
    // array_any: does at least one element satisfy the condition?
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function patientInfo(array $rights, ?ScheduleView $schedule): ?string
    {
        if ($rights['patient'] === null || $rights['patientCanBook']) {
            return null;
        }
        $appointmentShown = $schedule !== null && array_any($schedule->rows, fn (ScheduleRow $r) => $r->mine);
        return $appointmentShown ? null : 'SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO';
    }
}

The application’s main page. The header comment summarizes what each user sees and can do. The [#[Route('/schedule')]] attribute of the class (line 66) specifies the start of the path for all its routes (example 02): the route [''] is [/schedule] itself.

docs.title: 11.19.3.1. The URL on the page
docs.text: The entire page is described by its URL: [/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-26] displays Doctor 1’s schedule for that day; [&book=4] also opens the booking window for slot 4. You can reload the page, bookmark it, or use the browser’s Back button without a single line of [JavaScript]. The form at the top of the page (for selecting the doctor and the day) is a GET form (example 17): it reloads the page with new parameters. The appointment booking window is opened by a simple link and closed by a link to the same page without the [book] parameter.

docs.title: 11.19.3.2. GET /schedule
docs.text:
Lines 81–154:

  • the parameters of URL are read as-is ([$request->query->get('day')]), without validation by [Symfony]: a missing parameter ([null]) is not an error (the system defaults to today or “no doctor”); an invalid date is an error, displayed at the bottom of the page (the doctor and day selections remain visible, but the calendar is not displayed); a doctor or time slot number that is not a positive integer is simply ignored;
  • a logged-in user who has not selected a doctor sees their schedule: their doctor is retrieved via their account ([getDoctorByUserId]). [?->getId()]: the nullsafe operator returns [null] if the object is [null], instead of raising an error;
  • the drop-down list of doctors: [array_map] converts each doctor to [OptionView];
  • the calendar, formatted and filtered according to the user’s permissions ([scheduleView], below);
  • the booking window, only if the requested time slot is bookable by that user: a patient who attempts to generate the URL [&book=2] for a booked time slot would get nothing. [array_find] (example 06) returns the first element of an array that satisfies a condition, or [null]. The list of patients is provided only to the administrator and doctors; a patient receives only their own name;
  • the view receives its variables ([render], example 13), including [pageTitle] and [error], which are read by the template.

docs.title: 11.19.3.3. POST /schedule/book
docs.text:
Lines 167–215:

  • the anti-CSRF token, followed by the hidden fields from the booking form (doctor, day, time slot). Since these are invalid, this must be a manually crafted request: [BadRequestHttpException], the “invalid request” page (400);
  • For a patient, the field [clientId] is ignored: the patient always makes an appointment for themselves ([Utils::connectedPatient]). Relying on a field sent by the browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation on behalf of someone else. For the administrator and doctors, a patient must have been selected; otherwise, the reservation window reopens with a message;
  • the time slot must belong to the doctor listed on the page;
  • the business rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment, available time slot) are verified by the business logic layer. A [BusinessException] becomes a flash error message; its public properties [key] and [params] provide the message. The same rejection—“one upcoming appointment”—is phrased in the second person for the patient themselves (“You already have…”). Any other exception is not intercepted: this is a true error (500 page);
  • in all cases, the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (example 20): a pop-up message and a redirect to the calendar.

docs.title: 11.19.3.4. POST /schedule/cancel
docs.text: Lines 221–239: Cancellation of an appointment by the administrator or a doctor (rule [^/schedule/cancel$] derived from [security.yaml]). An appointment that no longer exists (already canceled by someone else, or due to a double-click) is not an error: it’s just a message.

docs.title: 11.19.3.5. Permissions, the formatted calendar, and utility functions
docs.text:
• lines 247–255: what the user is authorized to do on the page, in an associative array: is the user an administrator (ADMIN or DOCTOR)? a patient (and which one)? can this patient make a reservation (no upcoming appointments)?
  • Lines 260–285: The doctor’s schedule, converted into rows for the view. The privacy consideration is on line 278: a patient sees only the name associated with their own appointment. For the others, the property [patient] is set to [null], and the view displays “Booked.” The name is not hidden by the view: it is never passed to the view, and therefore does not appear in the page’s source code, where it would be easy to read it. The “Book” button is displayed for an available time slot, on a day that has not yet passed, to an administrator or a patient who can make a reservation; the “Cancel” button is displayed only to administrators. The named arguments ([slotId: $slot->getId()]) make the construction of an object with eight properties readable;
  • lines 291–296: the hidden fields of the POST forms. [[$doctorId, $day] = ...] (lines 171 and 225) breaks down the rendered array into two variables;
  • lines 300–307: the URL for a doctor’s schedule on a given day. [generateUrl('schedule', [...])] adds the values that are not path parameters to the end of URL as query parameters: [/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-26];
  • lines 321–328: the message explaining to a patient why there is no “Book” button (they already have an upcoming appointment), unless that appointment is in the displayed calendar (immediately after booking it, the message would be moved). [array_any] ([PHP] 8.4): Does at least one element satisfy the condition?

docs.title: 11.19.4. src/Controller/PersonsController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/PersonsController.php: the management of the doctors and that of the
// clients (reserved to the ADMIN) are IDENTICAL: same list, same form,
// same rules. Rather than writing the same actions twice, we write them
// once in this ABSTRACT class; DoctorsController and ClientsController
// inherit from it, and only specify what distinguishes them: the name of the section
// (doctors or clients), the translation keys, and the methods of
// the ApplicationModel to call.
//
// The #[Route] attributes of the actions are inherited too: the #[Route] attribute
// of EACH child class gives them the beginning of their path (/doctors or
// /clients) and of their name (doctors_ or clients_). We thus get, for each one:
//
//   GET  /doctors                    list                      doctors_list
//   GET  /doctors/add                empty form                doctors_add
//   POST /doctors/add                creation                  doctors_add
//   GET  /doctors/{id}/edit          pre-filled form           doctors_edit
//   POST /doctors/{id}/edit          modification              doctors_edit
//   POST /doctors/{id}/delete        deletion                  doctors_delete
//
// (and the same URLs under /clients). The views are common too:
// templates/persons/list.html.twig and persons/form.html.twig.
//
// SECURITY: the access_control rule ^/(doctors|clients) of
// config/packages/security.yaml reserves all these URLs to the ADMIN - including those
// that would be added later.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Person;
use App\Form\PersonFieldsType;
use App\Form\PersonType;
use App\Business\PersonData;
use App\Business\BusinessException;
use App\Views\PersonKeys;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use App\Web\BaseController;
use App\Web\Flash;
use App\Web\Message;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

abstract class PersonsController extends BaseController
{
    // the form fields concerned by each "input" business error (a
    // duplicate): they are framed in red, the message being at the bottom of the page
    public const BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS = [
        'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN' => ['login'],
        'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS' => ['first_name', 'last_name'],
        'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS' => ['first_name', 'last_name'],
    ];

    public function __construct(protected ApplicationModel $application, protected Flash $flash)
    {
    }

    // ---- what each type of person must provide

    // "doctors" or "clients": the beginning of the names of the routes
    abstract protected function section(): string;

    abstract protected function keys(): PersonKeys;

    /** @return list<Person> */
    abstract protected function all(): array;

    abstract protected function find(int $id): ?Person;

    abstract protected function create(PersonData $data): Person;

    abstract protected function update(int $id, PersonData $data): Person;

    abstract protected function erase(int $id): void;

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /doctors (or /clients)
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('', name: 'list', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function list(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('persons/list.html.twig', ['pageTitle' => $this->keys()->title,
            'keys' => $this->keys(), 'section' => $this->section(), 'persons' => $this->all()]);
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /doctors/add: the empty form; POST: the creation
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/add', name: 'add', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function add(Request $request): Response
    {
        $form = $this->createForm(PersonType::class, ['title' => 'Mr']);
        $form->handleRequest($request);
        if ($form->isSubmitted() && $form->isValid()) {
            try {
                $person = $this->create(PersonFieldsType::data($form->getData()));
            } catch (BusinessException $e) {
                return $this->businessError($e, $form, null);
            }
            $this->flash->success($this->keys()->added, self::params($person));
            return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_list');
        }
        return $this->page($form, null);
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /doctors/{id}/edit: the pre-filled form; POST: the modification.
    // {id<\d+>}: a parameter made of digits (see example 02):
    // /doctors/abc/edit matches no route (404 page)
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/{id<\d+>}/edit', name: 'edit', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function edit(Request $request, int $id): Response
    {
        $person = $this->find($id) ?? throw $this->createNotFoundException();
        // the form, pre-filled with the values of the person (the
        // password, on the other hand, is never displayed)
        $form = $this->createForm(PersonType::class, [
            'title' => $person->getTitle(), 'first_name' => $person->getFirstName(),
            'last_name' => $person->getLastName(), 'login' => $person->getAccount()->getLogin(),
            'version' => $person->getVersion(),
        ], ['creation' => false]);
        $form->handleRequest($request);
        if ($form->isSubmitted() && $form->isValid()) {
            try {
                $person = $this->update($id, PersonFieldsType::data($form->getData()));
            } catch (BusinessException $e) {
                return $this->businessError($e, $form, $person);
            }
            $this->flash->success($this->keys()->edited, self::params($person));
            return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_list');
        }
        return $this->page($form, $person);
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /doctors/{id}/delete
    // (the confirmation "Are you sure?" is asked before the form is sent,
    // see public/js/app.js)
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/{id<\d+>}/delete', name: 'delete', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function delete(Request $request, int $id): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        $person = $this->find($id);
        try {
            $this->erase($id);
            $this->flash->success($this->keys()->deleted, self::params($person));
        } catch (BusinessException $e) {
            $this->flash->error($e->key, $e->params);
        }
        return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_list');
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

    // $person null: creation form; otherwise: modification form.
    // A refused form (invalid input, or business rule): the code 422
    private function page(FormInterface $form, ?Person $person, ?Message $error = null,
        array $invalidFields = []): Response
    {
        $keys = $this->keys();
        $refused = $error !== null || ($form->isSubmitted() && ! $form->isValid());
        return $this->render('persons/form.html.twig', [
            'pageTitle' => $person === null ? $keys->add : $keys->edit,
            'form' => $form,
            'error' => $error,
            'invalidFields' => $invalidFields,
            'listUrl' => $this->generateUrl($this->section().'_list'),
        ], new Response(status: $refused ? 422 : 200));
    }

    // a business rule refused the write: the form is displayed again, with
    // the user's input (without the password), the message of the business
    // layer (at the bottom of the page), and the fields concerned, if any, framed in
    // red so that the user immediately sees what to correct
    private function businessError(BusinessException $e, FormInterface $form, ?Person $person): Response
    {
        if (in_array($e->key, ['ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND', 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND'], true)) {
            // deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: back to the list
            $this->flash->error($e->key, $e->params);
            return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_list');
        }
        return $this->page($form, $person, new Message($e->key, $e->params),
            self::BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS[$e->key] ?? []);
    }

    // {name} and {login} of the messages "added / updated / deleted"
    private static function params(?Person $person): array
    {
        return $person === null ? ['name' => '', 'login' => '']
            : ['name' => "{$person->getFirstName()} {$person->getLastName()}",
                'login' => $person->getAccount()->getLogin()];
    }
}

The management of doctors and clients is identical: same list, same form, same rules. The actions are written once, in an abstract class; [DoctorsController] and [ClientsController] inherit from it. Each must provide what sets it apart: this is the role of the abstract methods in lines 64–77, declared without code; a child class that does not implement them would be rejected by [PHP]. This is the design pattern known as the “template method”: the parent class defines the algorithm, and the child classes provide the details.

The [#[Route]] attributes of the actions are also inherited. [Symfony] ignores the abstract class but examines the methods of each of the child classes, including inherited ones; the [#[Route]] attribute of the child class specifies the start of their path and name: the action [list] becomes the routes [doctors_list] ([/doctors]) and [clients_list] ([/clients]). To add an action to the doctor management or client management modules, simply write it here.

  • Lines 51–55: the fields affected by each business-logic input error: a duplicate login affects the “login” field; a name match affects the “first name” and “last name” fields. These fields will be highlighted in red;
  • line 57: the constructor, inherited by the child classes. Its properties are [protected]: visible to the child classes;
  • Lines 82–87: the list. This view is common to both sections: it receives the translation keys for the section ([keys]) and its name ([section]), which is used to generate the route names ([section ~ '_add'] in the view);
  • Lines 92–107: Adding. A single action for GET (the empty form, with the title [Mr] selected) and POST (creation), as in Example 19. An invalid entry reloads the form. A valid entry proceeds to the business layer, which may reject the write operation (e.g., a namesake, a login already in use); otherwise, a success message appears and the user returns to the list (schema PRG);
  • lines 114–136: the update, for an existing person: [?? throw $this->createNotFoundException()] (the 404 page; [throw] is an expression that can be used to the right of [??]). [{id<\d+>}] (line 114) accepts only digits for the parameter [{id}] (example: 02). The form is pre-filled with the person’s values and their version; [handleRequest] replaces them with the entered data, resulting in POST;
  • lines 143–155: deletion. The form requested confirmation in the browser (example 21). The person’s information is retrieved before deletion to generate the success message (“Doctor Paul TATOU has been deleted.”);
  • lines 161–173: the form, either for creation ([$person] equals [null]) or modification. A rejected form (invalid input or business rule violation) is returned with status code 422 (example 19). The view receives the form itself ([render] converts it into a “form view,” example 18);
  • lines 179–188: the business layer rejected the write operation. If a person has been deleted in the meantime (by another administrator), the user is returned to the list. Otherwise, the form is redisplayed directly (without redirection), as in the case of an input error: it already contains the user’s input. Added to this are the message from the business layer (displayed at the bottom of the page, in the error area) and the fields to be highlighted in red. Note that the entity manager is closed after the exception (the business layer, as mentioned above): the action now only displays;
  • lines 191–196: the parameters [{name}] and [{login}] for the success messages.
