docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/DoctorsController.php: the management of the doctors (ADMIN role
// only). All the actions are written by PersonsController: all that
// remains here is to say WHAT to call and WHICH labels to display.

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Person;
use App\Business\PersonData;
use App\Views\PersonKeys;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

// the beginning of the path and of the name of all the routes inherited from PersonsController
#[Route('/doctors', name: 'doctors_')]
class DoctorsController extends PersonsController
{
    protected function section(): string
    {
        return 'doctors';
    }

    // DOCTORS.TITLE, DOCTORS.ADD... (see translations)
    protected function keys(): PersonKeys
    {
        return PersonKeys::of('DOCTORS');
    }

    protected function all(): array
    {
        return $this->application->getAllDoctors();
    }

    protected function find(int $id): ?Person
    {
        return $this->application->getDoctorById($id);
    }

    protected function create(PersonData $data): Person
    {
        return $this->application->addDoctor($data);
    }

    protected function update(int $id, PersonData $data): Person
    {
        return $this->application->editDoctor($id, $data);
    }

    protected function erase(int $id): void
    {
        $this->application->deleteDoctor($id);
    }
}

All that remains here is to specify which methods to call (the methods of [ApplicationModel]) and which labels to display (the [DOCTORS.xxx] keys in the dictionaries), and to provide the starting paths and route names (line 14). [ApplicationModel] is located in the [$this->application] property, declared by the parent class’s constructor. [ClientsController] is identical, with the client methods and the [CLIENTS.xxx] keys.

docs.title: 11.19.6. src/Controller/RegistrationController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/RegistrationController.php: "Create a patient account": a patient
// who does not have an account yet creates it themselves. PUBLIC routes (one does not
// have an account yet, by definition):
//
//   POST /register/access     "Create a patient account" button of the login
//                             page: checks the captcha of THAT
//                             page, then opens the form
//   GET  /register            the form
//   POST /register            the creation, then back to the login page
//
// The path is protected against robots by ONE captcha, that of the login
// page:
//   1. the "Create a patient account" button sends the login form to
//      /register/access; if the captcha is copied correctly, the server issues a
//      pass (see src/Security/RegistrationPass.php);
//   2. without a valid pass, /register sends back to the login
//      page (#[RegistrationPassRequired] attribute, see
//      src/EventListener/CheckRegistrationPass.php);
//   3. the pass is consumed at the creation: one solved captcha allows creating
//      ONE account;
//   4. in addition, the number of accounts created per hour and per IP address is limited
//      (see src/Security/AttemptLimiter.php).
//
// The account created is exactly the one the ADMIN would create from the "Patients" page
// (same method of the business layer: addClient), except that the patient
// CHOOSES their login and their password (required, with confirmation).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Form\PersonFieldsType;
use App\Form\RegistrationType;
use App\Business\BusinessException;
use App\Security\CaptchaService;
use App\Security\AttemptLimiter;
use App\Security\RegistrationPass;
use App\Security\RegistrationPassRequired;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use App\Web\BaseController;
use App\Web\Flash;
use App\Web\Message;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route('/register')]
class RegistrationController extends BaseController
{
    public function __construct(
        private ApplicationModel $application,
        private CaptchaService $captchas,
        private AttemptLimiter $limiter,
        private RegistrationPass $passes,
        private Flash $flash,
    ) {
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /register/access   fields: captchaId, captcha (those of the login
    // page; login and password, also sent, are ignored)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/access', name: 'registration_access', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function access(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        $ip = (string) $request->getClientIp();

        // too many accounts created recently from this address: no point going further
        $minutes = $this->limiter->registrationBlockMinutes($ip);
        if ($minutes > 0) {
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS', ['minutes' => $minutes]);
            return $this->redirectToRoute('login');
        }

        // missing or wrong captcha: back to the login page, with a
        // new image (a failure counts as a login failure)
        if (! $this->captchas->verify($request->request->getString('captchaId'),
            $request->request->getString('captcha'))) {
            $this->limiter->loginFailure($ip, '');
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
            return $this->redirectToRoute('login');
        }

        // correct captcha: the pass is issued and the form is opened
        $response = $this->redirectToRoute('registration');
        $response->headers->setCookie($this->passes->issue());
        return $response;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /register: the form; POST /register: the creation. The
    // pass has been checked BEFORE the call of the action (#[RegistrationPassRequired]).
    // The form validates ALL the input (fields and password confirmation):
    // the user corrects all their errors in one go
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('', name: 'registration', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    #[RegistrationPassRequired]
    public function register(Request $request): Response
    {
        $form = $this->createForm(RegistrationType::class, ['title' => 'Mr']);
        $form->handleRequest($request);
        if (! $form->isSubmitted() || ! $form->isValid()) {
            return $this->page($form);
        }
        $ip = (string) $request->getClientIp();

        // 1. too many accounts created recently from this address?
        $minutes = $this->limiter->registrationBlockMinutes($ip);
        if ($minutes > 0) {
            return $this->page($form, new Message('ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS', ['minutes' => $minutes]));
        }

        // 2. the creation (client + USER account, in a transaction)
        $data = PersonFieldsType::data($form->getData());
        try {
            $this->application->addClient($data);
        } catch (BusinessException $e) {
            // login or first + last names already taken: the pass remains valid
            return $this->page($form, new Message($e->key, $e->params),
                PersonsController::BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS[$e->key] ?? []);
        }

        // 3. the pass has been used: it will not allow creating a 2nd account
        $this->passes->consume($request->cookies->get(RegistrationPass::COOKIE));
        $this->limiter->registrationSuccess($ip);

        // 4. back to the login page, login pre-filled
        $this->flash->success('REGISTRATION.DONE', ['login' => $data->login]);
        return RegistrationPass::clearCookie($this->redirectToRoute('login', ['login' => $data->login]));
    }

    // the form; a refused form: the code 422
    private function page(FormInterface $form, ?Message $error = null, array $invalidFields = []): Response
    {
        $refused = $error !== null || ($form->isSubmitted() && ! $form->isValid());
        return $this->render('registration.html.twig', ['pageTitle' => 'REGISTRATION.TITLE',
            'form' => $form, 'error' => $error, 'invalidFields' => $invalidFields],
            new Response(status: $refused ? 422 : 200));
    }
}

The patient creates a patient account themselves. The flow is protected by a CAPTCHA, the same one used on the login page.

  • Lines 65–91: The “Create a patient account” button on the login page submits the login form to this address (later, the view [login]). If too many accounts have been created recently from this address (IP), there’s no need to proceed further. If the CAPTCHA is missing or incorrect: return to the login page with a new image and a message; the failure counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username). If the CAPTCHA is correct: a token is stored in a cookie, and the user is redirected to the form;
  • lines 99–107: the form. The [#[RegistrationPassRequired]] attribute (line 100) causes the token to be verified by the listener [CheckRegistrationPass] before the action is called. The form validates all input, including the password confirmation: the user sees all errors at once;
  • Lines 108–132: creation. The client and their account are created using the same business-layer method as for the administrator ([addClient]); only the username and password are chosen by the patient. If a username or a homonym is already taken: return to the form without consuming the pass. Creating an account consumes the token (one solved CAPTCHA equals one account), counts toward the hourly limit, and redirects to the login page with the username pre-filled ([redirectToRoute('login', ['login' => ...])] adds the parameter [?login=...]), along with a success message. The pass cookie is cleared.

docs.title: 11.19.7. src/Controller/PatientAreaController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/PatientAreaController.php: the PERSONAL pages of the patient (role
// USER), the one they see right after logging in:
//
//   GET  /my-area                  home page: [Manage my account], [View a
//                                  schedule], and their upcoming appointment
//   POST /my-area/cancel           cancels THEIR appointment
//   GET  /my-account               modification form of their account
//   POST /my-account               modification
//   POST /my-account/delete        deletion of the account (and of its appointments)
//
// Golden rule of this controller: the patient concerned is ALWAYS that of the token
// ($this->utils->connectedPatient()), never an identifier sent by the
// browser. A patient can therefore neither see, nor modify, nor cancel what
// belongs to another patient, even by building their requests themselves.
//
// Any modification or deletion of the account requires the CURRENT password:
// someone who found a session left open could neither change the
// password, nor delete the account. The current password errors are
// counted as login failures (same limit).
//
// Security: all these URLs are reserved to the USER role (rule ^/my- of
// config/packages/security.yaml).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Appointment;
use App\Form\PersonFieldsType;
use App\Form\MyAccountType;
use App\Business\BusinessException;
use App\Security\AuthService;
use App\Security\AttemptLimiter;
use App\Views\AppointmentView;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use App\Web\BaseController;
use App\Web\Flash;
use App\Web\Message;
use App\Web\Utils;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormError;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
use Symfony\Contracts\Translation\TranslatorInterface;

class PatientAreaController extends BaseController
{
    public function __construct(
        private ApplicationModel $application,
        private AuthService $auth,
        private AttemptLimiter $limiter,
        private Utils $utils,
        private Flash $flash,
        private TranslatorInterface $translator,
    ) {
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /my-area
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/my-area', name: 'area', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function area(): Response
    {
        $patient = $this->utils->connectedPatient();
        $appointments = array_map(fn (Appointment $a) => new AppointmentView(
            $a->getId(),
            $this->utils->formatDay($a->getDay()),
            $a->getSlot()->time(),
            $a->getSlot()->getDoctor()->label(),
            // link to the doctor's schedule on that day: the patient sees their name there
            $this->generateUrl('schedule', ['doctorId' => $a->getSlot()->getDoctor()->getId(),
                'day' => Utils::iso($a->getDay())])),
            $this->application->getClientUpcomingAppointments($patient->getId()));
        return $this->render('area.html.twig', ['pageTitle' => 'AREA.TITLE',
            'patient' => $patient->label(), 'appointments' => $appointments]);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /my-area/cancel   field: appointmentId
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/my-area/cancel', name: 'area_cancel', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function cancelAppointment(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        $patient = $this->utils->connectedPatient();
        $appointmentId = Utils::positiveInteger($request->request->get('appointmentId'));
        $appointment = $appointmentId !== null ? $this->application->getAppointmentById($appointmentId) : null;
        // an appointment that does not exist, and that of ANOTHER patient, receive the
        // same answer: nothing is revealed about the appointments of the others
        if ($appointment === null || $appointment->getClient()->getId() !== $patient->getId()) {
            $this->flash->error('ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND');
        } else {
            $this->application->deleteAppointment($appointment);
            $this->flash->success('SCHEDULE.CANCELLED');
        }
        return $this->redirectToRoute('area');
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /my-account: the form, pre-filled with the values of the patient;
    // POST /my-account: the modification
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/my-account', name: 'account', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function account(Request $request): Response
    {
        $patient = $this->utils->connectedPatient();
        $form = $this->createForm(MyAccountType::class, [
            'title' => $patient->getTitle(), 'first_name' => $patient->getFirstName(), 'last_name' => $patient->getLastName(),
            'login' => $patient->getAccount()->getLogin(), 'version' => $patient->getVersion(),
        ]);
        $form->handleRequest($request);
        if (! $form->isSubmitted() || ! $form->isValid()) {
            return $this->page($form);
        }

        // the current password; wrong: the message goes UNDER the field (an error
        // added to the field, FormError), and at the bottom of the page
        $error = $this->checkCurrentPassword($request, $patient,
            $form->get('current_password')->getData());
        if ($error !== null) {
            $form->get('current_password')->addError(
                new FormError($this->translator->trans($error->key, $error->params)));
            return $this->page($form, $error);
        }

        try {
            $client = $this->application->editClient($patient->getId(),
                PersonFieldsType::data($form->getData()));
        } catch (BusinessException $e) {
            return $this->page($form, new Message($e->key, $e->params),
                PersonsController::BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS[$e->key] ?? []);
        }
        // the login and the displayed name are IN the token: a new one is issued,
        // otherwise the navigation bar would keep the old name
        $this->flash->success('MY_ACCOUNT.UPDATED');
        $response = $this->redirectToRoute('area');
        $response->headers->setCookie($this->auth->tokenCookie($client->getAccount()));
        return $response;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /my-account/delete   field: current_password
    // The account, the client and ALL their appointments disappear together, then the
    // patient is logged out.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[Route('/my-account/delete', name: 'account_delete', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function deleteAccount(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->checkCsrf($request);
        $patient = $this->utils->connectedPatient();
        $error = $this->checkCurrentPassword($request, $patient,
            $request->request->getString('current_password'));
        if ($error !== null) {
            $this->flash->error($error->key, $error->params);
            return $this->redirectToRoute('account');
        }
        $this->application->deleteClient($patient->getId());
        $this->flash->success('MY_ACCOUNT.DELETED');
        return AuthService::clearCookie($this->redirectToRoute('login'));
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

    // the account page; a refused form: the code 422
    private function page(FormInterface $form, ?Message $error = null, array $invalidFields = []): Response
    {
        $refused = $error !== null || ($form->isSubmitted() && ! $form->isValid());
        return $this->render('account.html.twig', ['pageTitle' => 'MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE',
            'form' => $form, 'error' => $error, 'invalidFields' => $invalidFields],
            new Response(status: $refused ? 422 : 200));
    }

    // null if the current password is correct; otherwise the error message
    private function checkCurrentPassword(Request $request, Client $patient, ?string $password): ?Message
    {
        $ip = (string) $request->getClientIp();
        $login = $patient->getAccount()->getLogin();
        $minutes = $this->limiter->loginBlockMinutes($ip, $login);
        if ($minutes > 0) {
            return new Message('ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', ['minutes' => $minutes]);
        }
        if (! $password || $this->auth->validate($login, $password) === null) {
            $this->limiter->loginFailure($ip, $login);
            return new Message('ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD');
        }
        return null;
    }
}

The patient’s personal pages. The golden rule for this controller: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token ([Utils::connectedPatient]), never an identifier sent by the browser. A patient cannot therefore view, modify, or cancel information belonging to another patient, even by crafting their own requests.

  • lines 64–79: My area: the patient’s name and their upcoming appointments, formatted ([AppointmentView]), each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day;
  • lines 84–100: the cancellation of his appointment. Both a nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments (not even their existence);
  • lines 106–117: the “Manage my account” form, pre-filled with the patient’s information, and its submission;
  • lines 119–142: the modification. Any modification requires the current password: someone who found a session left open would be unable to change the password or do anything else. If the current password is incorrect, the form is redisplayed, with the message below the field and at the bottom of the page. [addError(new FormError(...))] adds an error to a field, as if the validation had detected it (example 18); its message is text that has already been translated, hence the translation received by the builder ([TranslatorInterface], example 22). After the modification, a new token is generated: the login and the displayed name are included in the token, and the navigation bar would otherwise retain the old name until the next login;
  • lines 149–163: deletion of the account, the client, and all their appointments, using the same business-logic method as for the administrator. This second form on the page is hand-coded (a single field, the current password), with the application’s anti-CSRF token. The patient is then logged out (the token cookie is cleared);
  • lines 177–190: Verification of the current password. This is subject to the attempt limiter, just like a login: without this, someone with an open session could try thousands of passwords via the “Manage my account” form and discover the correct one.

docs.title: 11.20. The Views
docs.text: The [Twig] views in the [templates] folder: a template, fragments, macros, and pages.

docs.title: 11.20.1.1. templates/layout.html.twig
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
{# =========================================================================
   templates/layout.html.twig
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   The layout COMMON to all the pages (see example 15): each page
   (schedule.html.twig, login.html.twig...) EXTENDS it ({% extends %}) and fills its
   [content] block.

   Twig ESCAPES everything it displays with {{ ... }} (the characters < > & " '
   become < >...): protection against HTML injection through an entered
   name, for example. To insert HTML as is, it must be requested
   explicitly (raw filter, see fragments/captcha.html.twig).

   Messages: a success is displayed at the TOP of the page, an error at the BOTTOM, on a light
   pink background (errors fragment).

   The layout shares the variables of the page: [pageTitle] (the key of the title of
   the page, passed by the action). The language of the page is that of the request
   (app.request.locale, see src/EventListener/SetLanguage.php).
   ========================================================================= #}
<html lang="{{ app.request.locale }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  {# pageTitle|trans: the translation of a key; here, the key is a VARIABLE #}
  <title>{{ pageTitle|trans }} - {{ 'APP.TITLE'|trans }}</title>
  {# asset(): the URL of a file of the public folder #}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css') }}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('css/styles.css') }}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include 'fragments/navbar.html.twig' %}
    {% include 'fragments/success.html.twig' %}
    <main>
      {% block content %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% include 'fragments/errors.html.twig' %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" dialog, hidden as long as it is not needed #}
  {% include 'fragments/confirmation.html.twig' %}
  <script src="{{ asset('js/app.js') }}"></script>
</body>
</html>

The template common to all pages (Example 15): each page extends it ([{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}]) and fills in its [content] block (line 36).

  • Line 21: the page’s language, [fr] or [en]: the language of the request, set by the listener [SetLanguage]. [app] is the global variable that [Symfony] provides to all views (Example 15);
  • line 26: the page title, translated: [pageTitle|trans] translates the key contained in the variable [pageTitle], which each action passes to its view;
  • lines 28–29: the function [asset] returns the URL from a file in the [public] folder (Example 15);
  • lines 33–38: the navigation bar, the success messages at the top of the page, the page content, and the error area at the bottom of the page. These fragments are inserted by [{% include %}] (Example 15): they access the page’s variables;
  • lines 41–42: the “Are you sure?” window, hidden until needed, and the script that displays it.

[Twig] escapes everything it displays using [{{ ... }}] (Example 13): an entered name containing HTML ([<script>]) is displayed as-is, without being interpreted. This is protection against the effortless injection of HTML (XSS) into all pages.

docs.title: 11.20.1.2. templates/fragments/navbar.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/navbar.html.twig - the navigation bar.

   Title, FR/EN, role, name, logout - and a menu whose entries depend
   on the role: "Doctors" and "Patients" only appear for the ADMIN. It is
   only a display convenience: the real protection is the access rules
   (a USER who types /doctors by hand gets a 403 page). A patient (USER)
   also has their "My area" menu.

   user(): the logged-in user, or null (see src/Twig/ViewsExtension.php).
   The menu of the current page is highlighted ("active" class): it is if
   the path of the URL (app.request.pathInfo) begins with ([starts with]) one of the
   prefixes of the entry. The entries of the menu: a list of arrays [name of the
   route, key of the label, prefixes of the paths for which the entry is active].
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set user = user() %}
{% set menu = [] %}
{% if user %}
  {% if user.isPatient %}
    {# active for /my-area AND /my-account #}
    {% set menu = menu|merge([['area', 'APP.MENU_MY_AREA', ['/my-']]]) %}
  {% endif %}
  {% set menu = menu|merge([['schedule', 'APP.MENU_SCHEDULE', ['/schedule']]]) %}
  {% if user.isAdmin %}
    {% set menu = menu|merge([['doctors_list', 'APP.MENU_DOCTORS', ['/doctors']],
                              ['clients_list', 'APP.MENU_PATIENTS', ['/clients']]]) %}
  {% endif %}
{% endif %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">{{ 'APP.TITLE'|trans }}</span>

  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {# entry[0]: the name of the route; filter keeps the matching prefixes #}
    {% for entry in menu %}
    {% set active = entry[2]|filter(p => app.request.pathInfo starts with p) is not empty %}
    <li class="nav-item">
      <a class="nav-link{{ active ? ' active' }}" href="{{ path(entry[0]) }}">{{ entry[1]|trans }}</a>
    </li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), the active language highlighted #}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code in ['fr', 'en'] %}
      <a class="btn {{ app.request.locale == code ? 'btn-light' : 'btn-outline-light' }}"
         href="{{ path('language', {code: code}) }}">{{ code|upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if user %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ user.role.value }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ user.name }}</span>
    {# logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and to the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="{{ path('logout') }}" class="m-0">
      <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{{ 'APP.LOGOUT'|trans }}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>

The navigation bar. The menu items depend on the role: “My area” for a patient, “Doctors” and “Patients” for the administrator. This is merely a convenience feature: the real protection comes from the rules [access_control] (a patient who types [/doctors] manually will receive a 403 page).

  • Line 16: the logged-in user, or [null], returned by the [user()] function in our extension;
  • Lines 17–28: The menu is generated by the [{% set %}] instructions, which produce a list of entries: the route name, the label key, and the path prefixes for which the entry is active. The filter [merge] returns a new list, consisting of the elements from the first list followed by those from the second (for two associative arrays, it combines their keys). [user.isPatient]: [Twig] calls the method [isPatient()]. The entry “My area” is active for [/my-area] and [/my-account] (prefix [/my-]). This is borderline with the “no logic in views” rule: however, this logic only affects the display and is used only here;
  • Lines 34–39: For each entry, [active] is true if the path of the requested URL ([app.request.pathInfo]) begins with ([starts with]) one of the entry’s prefixes. The filter [filter] retains only those elements of a list that satisfy a condition, written as an arrow function ([p => ...]);
  • lines 44–49: the buttons FR / EN, which are simple links ([/language/fr]), with the active language highlighted;
  • lines 51–59: for a logged-in user, their role ([user.role.value]: the enumeration case string), their name, and the logout button. Logout is a request POST: a form reduced to its button, with its anti-CSRF token ([csrf_token('rdvmedecins')], example 21).

docs.title: 11.20.1.3. templates/fragments/success.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/success.html.twig - the SUCCESS messages left by
   the previous action (appointment booked, doctor added...), displayed only
   once, at the top of the page (see src/Web/Flash.php). An ERROR flash
   message, on the other hand, is displayed at the bottom of the page, by the errors fragment.

   app.flashes('success'): the flash messages of that type (see example 20). Each
   message is a Message object: message.key|trans(message.params) is the text
   of the key, where {name}, {login}... are replaced by their values.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% for message in app.flashes('success') %}
<div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ message.key|trans(message.params) }}</div>
{% endfor %}

The success flash messages, set by the previous action ([Flash::success]), are read and removed from the session by [app.flashes('success')] (Example 20). Each is a [Message] object, translated here into the page’s language: [message.key|trans(message.params)]. [role="status"]: A screen reader announces the message.

docs.title: 11.20.1.4. templates/fragments/errors.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/errors.html.twig - the error zone, at the BOTTOM of each
   page, on a light pink background (class .error-zone, see public/css/styles.css).

   It groups the three possible sources of error:
     - [error]: the error of the displayed page (invalid date, captcha badly
       copied, login already taken...), passed by the action;
     - the error flash messages, left by the previous action before a
       redirection (slot already booked, deletion refused...);
     - the input errors of an invalid form (see example 19): their
       messages are displayed UNDER the fields; here, if there is no other
       message, a simple sentence "The form contains errors.".

   error ?? null: the variable does not exist in all the pages.
   role="alert": a screen reader announces the message as soon as the page is displayed,
   even if it is at the bottom.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set messages = app.flashes('errors') %}
{% if error ?? null %}
  {% set messages = [error]|merge(messages) %}
{% endif %}
{% if messages is empty and form is defined and form.vars.submitted and not form.vars.valid %}
  {% set messages = [{key: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM', params: []}] %}
{% endif %}
{% if messages is not empty %}
<div class="error-zone" role="alert">
  {% for message in messages %}
  <div>{{ message.key|trans(message.params) }}</div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
{% endif %}

The error area, at the bottom of each page, on a light pink background. It combines the three possible sources of error:

  • flash error messages, generated by the previous action (a time slot already reserved, an expired session, etc.);
  • the error on the displayed page ([error]), transmitted by the action: an invalid date, a misspelled CAPTCHA, a username already in use, etc.; placed at the top of the list. [error ?? null]: this variable does not exist on all pages; the operator [??] does not flag a nonexistent variable—it replaces it with [null];
  • Input errors in an invalid form (example 19): their messages are displayed below the fields; here, if there are no other messages, a simple phrase: “The form contains errors.” On a long form, this lets the user know they need to scroll back up. [form.vars]: the properties of the form view, including [submitted] (submitted?) and [valid] (valid?). The message is written as an associative array with the same keys as the properties of a [Message]: for [Twig], [message.key] refers to both the key of an array and the property of an object.

[role="alert"]: A screen reader announces the message as soon as the page is displayed, even if it is at the bottom. The area remains fixed at the bottom of the window when the page is long (see the stylesheet below).

docs.title: 11.20.1.5. templates/fragments/confirmation.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
     templates/fragments/confirmation.html.twig - the modal dialog
     "Are you sure?" (see example 21).

     It replaces the browser's window.confirm() box, which can neither be styled
     nor translated (its buttons stay in the language of the browser, not
     in that of the page).

     ONE SINGLE dialog for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first. Its labels
     are translated here, by the server, like the rest of the page; the small script
     public/js/app.js merely displays it, puts in it the message specific to the
     form (data-confirmation attribute), and sends the form if
     the user confirms.
     ========================================================================= #}
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="confirmation-modal-title" aria-describedby="confirmation-modal-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="confirmation-modal-title">{{ 'CONFIRMATION.TITLE'|trans }}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="no" aria-label="{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA'|trans }}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes
               "Cancel this appointment?", and a "Cancel" button would be ambiguous there #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">{{ 'CONFIRMATION.NO'|trans }}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">{{ 'CONFIRMATION.YES'|trans }}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The “Are you sure?” modal window from Example 21, which replaces the browser’s [window.confirm()] dialog box: this dialog box does not format correctly, and its buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s language. A single window for the entire page, initially hidden (class [d-none] derived from [Bootstrap]); its labels are translated by the server, just like the rest of the page. The [public/js/app.js] script displays it, places the message from the form to be confirmed inside it (its [data-confirmation] attribute), and submits the form if the user confirms. The "Decline" button is labeled “No, go back” rather than “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context.

docs.title: 11.20.1.6. templates/fragments/booking.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/booking.html.twig - the booking dialog of
   the schedule.

   The REAL Bootstrap classes of a modal dialog (.modal, .modal-backdrop...),
   made visible "hard-coded" (show d-block) rather than by Bootstrap's
   JavaScript. It is the SERVER that decides to display it (parameter &book=...
   of the URL), and closing it amounts to following a link to the same page without this
   parameter.

   The fragment directly reads the variables of the page that includes it
   (booking, doctorId, day, backUrl).
   ========================================================================= #}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="booking-title">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="{{ path('schedule_book') }}" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="booking-title">{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE'|trans }}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ backUrl }}" aria-label="{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA'|trans }}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT'|trans({time: booking.time}) }}</p>

        {# what the server must know in addition to the chosen patient #}
        <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ doctorId }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ day }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="slotId" value="{{ booking.slotId }}">

        {# a patient books for themselves: no list to choose from (and the
           server ignores a possible clientId anyway) #}
        {% if booking.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL'|trans }}</span>:
          <strong>{{ booking.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="clientId">{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL'|trans }}</label>
        <select id="clientId" name="clientId" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT'|trans }}</option>
          {% for client in booking.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ backUrl }}">{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL'|trans }}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM'|trans }}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

The calendar booking window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), but made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]), rather than through the [JavaScript] of [Bootstrap]: it is the server that decides to display it when URL contains [&book=...]. Closing it (using the X or the Cancel button) is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([backUrl]).

  • Lines 27–30: the anti-CSRF token, and what the server needs to know: the doctor, the day, and the time slot;
  • Lines 34–47: A patient enters their own name without selecting from a list (and the server ignores any [clientId] field anyway). The administrator and doctors select the patient from a list; [required] and [autofocus]: the browser requires a selection and places the cursor in the list.

docs.title: 11.20.1.7. templates/fragments/captcha.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/captcha.html.twig - the captcha of the login
   page (see src/Security/CaptchaService.php). It protects both
   the login and the access to account creation ("Create a patient
   account" button). It reads the [captcha] variable of the page.

   captcha.svg|raw: the SVG image is inserted AS IS in the page, without
   escaping. It is harmless here because this SVG is built by the server
   itself and contains nothing that comes from the user - we would NEVER do
   that with user input.

   The hidden field captchaId tells the server WHICH captcha to check; the right
   answer itself is never sent to the browser. "Another image" simply reloads
   the page (path('login'): the URL of the page, without its parameters).
   ========================================================================= #}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{{ 'CAPTCHA.LABEL'|trans }}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{{ 'CAPTCHA.IMAGE_ALT'|trans }}">{{ captcha.svg|raw }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{{ path('login') }}">{{ 'CAPTCHA.NEW_IMAGE'|trans }}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captchaId" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{{ 'CAPTCHA.HELP'|trans }}</div>
</div>

The CAPTCHA (example 27). [captcha.svg|raw] inserts the image SVG as-is, without escaping it: otherwise, the browser would display its code XML. This is safe here because this SVG is generated by the server and contains nothing provided by the user: we would never do this with user input. The hidden field [captchaId] tells the server which CAPTCHA to verify; the response itself is never sent to the browser. The “Another image” link reloads the login page—and thus the CAPTCHA.

docs.title: 11.20.2. Macros: templates/macros.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/macros.html.twig - the macros of the forms (see example 15).

   field(field, invalidFields): a field of a form of the Form component,
   with its label, its error message or its help (form_row, drawn by the
   Bootstrap 5 theme, see example 18). The field is framed in red (class
   is-invalid) if it has an input error (the theme handles it), or if a BUSINESS
   error designates it: its name is in the list [invalidFields] passed by
   the action (a login already taken...), the message being at the bottom of the page.
   The attributes of the field (maxlength...) are completed, not replaced: merge.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% macro field(field, invalidFields = []) %}
  {% set attr = field.vars.attr %}
  {% if field.vars.name in invalidFields %}
    {% set attr = attr|merge({class: (attr.class|default('') ~ ' is-invalid')|trim}) %}
  {% endif %}
  {{ form_row(field, {attr: attr}) }}
{% endmacro %}

{# the identity fields (title, first name, last name), common to three forms:
   ADMIN's doctor/client, "Create a patient account" and "Manage my account" #}
{% macro identity(form, invalidFields = []) %}
  {# import _self: the macros of THIS file, to call the field macro #}
  {% import _self as m %}
  {{ m.field(form.title, invalidFields) }}
  <div class="row g-3">
    <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.first_name, invalidFields) }}</div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.last_name, invalidFields) }}</div>
  </div>
{% endmacro %}

Two macros (Example 15), used by the three pages that display a “person” form.

  • Lines 12–18: A field in a Form component form, generated by [form_row] (Example 18): its label, input field, error message, or tooltip, along with the classes from the [Bootstrap] 5 theme declared in [config/packages/twig.yaml]. The theme highlights a field with an input error in red (class [is-invalid]). The macro also adds it to a field identified by an error from the business layer: the list [invalidFields] passed by the action ([PersonsController::BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS]). A username that is already taken is not an input error (it has the correct format), but the user needs to see which field to correct. [field.vars]: the field view properties, including its name ([name]) and its attributes HTML ([attr]); these are appended ([merge]), not replaced: the field retains its [maxlength]. The second parameter of [form_row] replaces the field view properties;
  • Lines 22–30: the identity fields, common to three forms: the title, followed by the first name and last name side by side (the grid from [Bootstrap]: [row], [col-sm-6]). A macro cannot see the other macros in its file: [{% import _self as m %}] (line 24) imports them.

docs.title: 11.20.3.1. templates/login.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/login.html.twig - the login form (see AuthController).
   An ordinary hand-written HTML <form>: the browser itself sends login,
   password and captcha answer in POST /login, without JavaScript. In case
   of failure, the server sends back THIS page, with the login already entered, a NEW
   captcha and the error, displayed at the bottom of the page by the layout.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ 'LOGIN.TITLE'|trans }}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{{ path('login_submit') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ 'LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL'|trans }}</label>
          {# autofocus: a boolean attribute, written if the condition is true, omitted
             otherwise. The cursor goes to the first field to fill in #}
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{ login }}" required{{ login == '' ? ' autofocus' }}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ 'LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL'|trans }}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required{{ login != '' ? ' autofocus' }}>
        </div>

        {% include 'fragments/captcha.html.twig' %}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{ 'LOGIN.SUBMIT'|trans }}</button>

        {# no account yet: a patient can create one themselves. It is NOT
           a simple link: it is a second submit button of THIS form,
           which goes to another address (formaction). The server checks the
           captcha above there before opening the account creation page (see
           RegistrationController). formnovalidate: the browser does not require
           login and password (useless to create an account). Enter in a
           field always triggers the FIRST button of the form, "Log in". #}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="{{ path('registration_access') }}" formnovalidate>{{ 'LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT'|trans }}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{{ 'LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT_HELP'|trans }}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        <span>{{ 'LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS'|trans }}</span>
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - <span>{{ 'LOGIN.DEMO_ADMIN'|trans }}</span></li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - <span>{{ 'LOGIN.DEMO_DOCTOR'|trans }}</span></li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - <span>{{ 'LOGIN.DEMO_USER'|trans }}</span></li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

The login form, a hand-coded [<form>], is sent via POST to [/login] (the path [login_submit]).

  • Lines 22–28: The entered username is redisplayed after a failed login attempt ([login]). The attribute [autofocus] places the cursor in the first field to be filled in: the username if it is empty, or the password otherwise (after a failed attempt or after creating an account). [{{ login == '' ? ' autofocus' }}]: The ternary operator without “else” returns an empty string if the condition is false;
  • line 31: the CAPTCHA;
  • lines 42–43: the “Create a patient account” button is not a link; it is a second button that submits the same form to a different address (button attribute [formaction]). The server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page ([RegistrationController::access]). [formnovalidate]: The browser does not require a username and password (attributes [required]), as they are not needed to create an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first form submission button: Log in.

docs.title: 11.20.3.2. templates/schedule.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/schedule.html.twig - the main page (see ScheduleController).
   Three blocks:
     1. the choice of the doctor and of the day;
     2. the schedule;
     3. the booking dialog (fragment booking).
   A possible error (invalid date, unknown doctor) is displayed at the bottom of
   the page by the layout (fragment errors).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block content %}
  {# 1. choice of the doctor and of the day: a GET form, which simply reloads
        this page with ?doctorId=...&day=... in the URL #}
  <form method="get" action="{{ path('schedule') }}" class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
      <div class="col-sm-5">
        <label class="form-label" for="doctorId">{{ 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL'|trans }}</label>
        <select id="doctorId" name="doctorId" class="form-select" required>
          <option value="">{{ 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR'|trans }}</option>
          {% for doctor in doctors %}
          <option value="{{ doctor.id }}"{{ doctor.selected ? ' selected' }}>{{ doctor.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-4">
        <label class="form-label" for="day">{{ 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL'|trans }}</label>
        <input id="day" name="day" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{ day }}" required>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-3">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{ 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_SCHEDULE'|trans }}</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>

  {# patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no "Book" button #}
  {% if info %}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    <span>{{ info|trans }}</span>
    <a href="{{ path('area') }}" class="alert-link">{{ 'APP.MENU_MY_AREA'|trans }}</a>
  </div>
  {% endif %}

  {# 2. the schedule #}
  {% if schedule %}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{ 'SCHEDULE.TITLE_PREFIX'|trans }} {{ schedule.day }} - {{ schedule.doctor }}</h5>

    {% if schedule.rows is not empty %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{{ 'SCHEDULE.COLUMN_SLOT'|trans }}</th>
          <th>{{ 'SCHEDULE.COLUMN_STATUS'|trans }}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for row in schedule.rows %}
        <tr{{ row.bookable ? ' class="free-slot"' }}>
          <td>{{ row.time }}</td>
          <td>
            {# [patient] is set only if the user has the right to see this
               name (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient for THEIR appointment) - otherwise,
               simply "Booked" #}
            {% if row.free %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">{{ 'SCHEDULE.FREE'|trans }}</span>
            {% elseif row.patient %}
            <span class="badge {{ row.mine ? 'text-bg-primary' : 'text-bg-secondary' }}">{{ row.patient }}</span>
            {% else %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{ 'SCHEDULE.BOOKED_BY_OTHER'|trans }}</span>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
          <td>
            {# the displayed buttons have been decided by the controller (bookable,
               appointmentId) according to the role of the user. "Book" is a simple
               link: it reopens this page with the booking dialog of this slot #}
            {% if row.bookable %}
            <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{ row.bookUrl }}">{{ 'SCHEDULE.BOOK'|trans }}</a>
            {% endif %}
            {# "Cancel" MODIFIES data: it is therefore a POST #}
            {% if row.appointmentId %}
            <form method="post" action="{{ path('schedule_cancel') }}" class="m-0"
                  data-confirmation="{{ 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM'|trans }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{ row.appointmentId }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ doctorId }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ day }}">
              <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{{ 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT'|trans }}</button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ 'SCHEDULE.NO_SLOTS'|trans }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  {% else %}
  <p class="text-muted">{{ 'SCHEDULE.EMPTY_STATE'|trans }}</p>
  {% endif %}

  {# 3. the booking dialog, only if the URL contains &book=... #}
  {% if booking %}
  {% include 'fragments/booking.html.twig' %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}

The main page. Three sections: selecting a doctor and a day, the calendar, and the booking window.

  • Lines 15–34: Selecting a doctor and a day: a GET form (Example 17), which reloads the page with [?doctorId=...&day=...] in the URL. The day is a [type="date"] field: the browser displays a calendar and sends the date in [yyyy-mm-dd] format, regardless of how it is displayed ([26/09/2026] in French);
  • lines 37–42: for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment, why there is no “Book” button;
  • lines 66–72: the slot status: Free (in green), the patient’s name (in blue for the appointment of the logged-in patient, in gray otherwise), or “Booked.” The view does not make any decisions: [row.patient] is only populated if the user has permission to view that name;
  • lines 78–80: “Book” is a simple link: it reopens the page with the booking window for that time slot ([row.bookUrl]). It does not modify anything: a GET is sufficient;
  • lines 82–91: “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form (example 21), with its anti-CSRF token, the appointment to be canceled, and information to return to the same page (the doctor, the day). The [data-confirmation] attribute causes the page’s script to request confirmation;
  • lines 106–108: the booking window, if requested by URL (and if the time slot is available for booking).

docs.title: 11.20.3.3. templates/persons/list.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/persons/list.html.twig - the list of the doctors OR of the clients
   (ADMIN). A single view for both: the keys of the labels specific to each one
   arrive in [keys], and [section] ("doctors" or "clients") gives the beginning of the
   names of the routes (see PersonsController): section ~ '_add' -> "doctors_add".
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block content %}
  <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
    <h4 class="mb-0">{{ keys.title|trans }}</h4>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="{{ path(section ~ '_add') }}">{{ keys.add|trans }}</a>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    {% if persons is not empty %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{{ 'PERSONS.COLUMN_TITLE'|trans }}</th>
          <th>{{ 'PERSONS.COLUMN_FIRSTNAME'|trans }}</th>
          <th>{{ 'PERSONS.COLUMN_LASTNAME'|trans }}</th>
          <th>{{ 'PERSONS.COLUMN_LOGIN'|trans }}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {# person.title: Twig calls the getter getTitle() (see example 13) #}
        {% for person in persons %}
        <tr>
          <td>{{ person.title }}</td>
          <td>{{ person.firstName }}</td>
          <td>{{ person.lastName }}</td>
          <td><code>{{ person.account.login }}</code></td>
          <td class="text-end">
            <div class="d-inline-flex gap-2">
              <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
                 href="{{ path(section ~ '_edit', {id: person.id}) }}">{{ 'PERSONS.EDIT'|trans }}</a>
              {# data-confirmation: a confirmation dialog will open before
                 the form is sent (see public/js/app.js) #}
              <form method="post" action="{{ path(section ~ '_delete', {id: person.id}) }}" class="m-0"
                    data-confirmation="{{ keys.confirmDelete|trans }}">
                <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
                <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{{ 'PERSONS.DELETE'|trans }}</button>
              </form>
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ keys.empty|trans }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

The list of doctors or clients: the labels specific to each one are translation keys ([keys]), and the route names are generated from the section name ([path(section ~ '_edit', {id: person.id})]: the operator [~] concatenates, resulting in [doctors_edit] or [clients_edit]). [person.account.login]: the account login, populated with the list (layer DAO). The Delete button is a POST form, with confirmation.

docs.title: 11.20.3.4. templates/persons/form.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/persons/form.html.twig - creation OR modification of a
   doctor or of a client (ADMIN), with the PersonType form.

   When the input is refused (empty field, login already taken...), the action
   displays THIS page again, and the view shows:
     - the values already entered (except the password);
     - the faulty fields framed in red (Bootstrap class "is-invalid");
     - under a field refused by validation, its message;
     - the error message of the page, AT THE BOTTOM of the page (errors fragment).
   form_start writes the <form> tag (POST method, URL of the page); form_end, the
   end of the form, with the fields that have not been written yet: the
   anti-CSRF token, and, in modification, the hidden version field (the optimistic lock).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ pageTitle|trans }}</h5>

      {{ form_start(form) }}
        {# form_errors: the errors of the form itself (wrong anti-CSRF token) #}
        {{ form_errors(form) }}
        {# title, first name, last name: a macro common to three forms #}
        {{ m.identity(form, invalidFields) }}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ 'PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION'|trans }}</h6>
        {{ m.field(form.login, invalidFields) }}
        {# never pre-filled: the password never goes back to the browser #}
        {{ m.field(form.password) }}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ 'PERSONS.SAVE'|trans }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ listUrl }}">{{ 'PERSONS.BACK'|trans }}</a>
        </div>
      {{ form_end(form) }}
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

Creating or editing a doctor or a client using the [PersonType] form.

  • Line 16: Importing macros under the name [m];
  • Line 24: [form_start] writes the tag [<form>]: the method POST, the page’s URL, and the attribute [novalidate] (type option [attr]);
  • line 26: [form_errors(form)] displays errors in the form itself that do not relate to any specific field: an invalid anti-CSRF token (“The page has expired...”);
  • line 28: title, first name, and last name, via the [identity] macro;
  • lines 31–33: the username and password, which are never pre-filled. Their tooltips differ between creation and modification (type options);
  • line 39: [form_end] closes the form after writing the fields that have not yet been written: the anti-CSRF token, and, when editing, the hidden version field (the optimistic lock).

docs.title: 11.20.3.5. templates/registration.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/registration.html.twig - "Create a patient account" (public page, see
   RegistrationController), with the RegistrationType form. Same identity
   fields as the ADMIN's form (identity macro), but the login and the
   password are required, with confirmation. No captcha HERE: one
   only reaches this page after having copied that of the login
   page ("Create a patient account" button).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-1">{{ 'REGISTRATION.TITLE'|trans }}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small mb-3">{{ 'REGISTRATION.INTRO'|trans }}</p>

      {{ form_start(form) }}
        {{ form_errors(form) }}
        {{ m.identity(form, invalidFields) }}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ 'PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION'|trans }}</h6>
        {{ m.field(form.login, invalidFields) }}
        {# the repeated field: its two inputs, side by side (first, second) #}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.password.first) }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.password.second) }}</div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-3">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ 'REGISTRATION.SUBMIT'|trans }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ path('login') }}">{{ 'REGISTRATION.BACK_TO_LOGIN'|trans }}</a>
        </div>
      {{ form_end(form) }}
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

Creating a patient account: the identity fields, followed by the username, password, and password confirmation, which are required. The two fields in the repeated field are [form.password.first] and [form.password.second] (lines 27–28), placed side by side. The password help text specifies the minimum length: “At least 6 characters.” There is no CAPTCHA here: you can only reach this page after entering the CAPTCHA from the login page.

docs.title: 11.20.3.6. templates/area.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/area.html.twig - "My area": the home page of the patient (USER
   role), displayed right after they log in.
     - two options: [Manage my account] and [View a schedule];
     - their upcoming appointment, if they have one, with the means to cancel it.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block content %}
  <h4 class="mb-3">{{ 'AREA.HELLO'|trans({name: patient}) }}</h4>

  <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="{{ path('account') }}">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{{ 'AREA.MANAGE_ACCOUNT'|trans }}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{{ 'AREA.MANAGE_ACCOUNT_HELP'|trans }}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="{{ path('schedule') }}">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{{ 'AREA.VIEW_SCHEDULE'|trans }}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{{ 'AREA.VIEW_SCHEDULE_HELP'|trans }}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{ 'AREA.MY_APPOINTMENT'|trans }}</h5>
    {# normally only one (rule "one upcoming appointment at a time"), but the
       page can display several. {% for %} ... {% else %}: a loop, and
       what is displayed if the list is empty; loop.last: last element? #}
    {% for appointment in appointments %}
    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-2 py-2{{ not loop.last ? ' border-bottom' }}">
      <div>
        <div class="fw-semibold">{{ appointment.day }}, {{ appointment.time }}</div>
        <div class="text-muted">
          <span>{{ appointment.doctor }}</span> -
          <a href="{{ appointment.scheduleUrl }}">{{ 'AREA.SEE_IN_SCHEDULE'|trans }}</a>
        </div>
      </div>
      <form method="post" action="{{ path('area_cancel') }}" class="m-0"
            data-confirmation="{{ 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM'|trans }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{ appointment.id }}">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger">{{ 'AREA.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT'|trans }}</button>
      </form>
    </div>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ 'AREA.NO_APPOINTMENT'|trans }}</p>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

“My area,” the patient’s home page: two large cards (“Manage my account,” “View a schedule”), and their upcoming appointment.

  • Lines 32–50: [{% for %}] ... [{% else %}] (Example 14) is a loop, followed by what to display if the list is empty. Normally, a patient has at most one upcoming appointment; however, the page is capable of displaying multiple appointments. [loop.last] (Example 14): the last item has no separator;
  • each appointment has a cancellation form (POST, with confirmation), which sends only its ID: the server will verify that it belongs to the logged-in patient.

docs.title: 11.20.3.7. templates/account.html.twig
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/account.html.twig - "Manage my account" (USER role).
   Two independent forms on the same page:
     1. the modification (identity, login, optional new password), with
        the MyAccountType form;
     2. the deletion of the account - which also cancels its appointments: a
        hand-written form.
   Both require the CURRENT password (current_password field).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. modification #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE'|trans }}</h5>

      {{ form_start(form) }}
        {{ form_errors(form) }}
        {{ m.identity(form, invalidFields) }}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ 'PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION'|trans }}</h6>
        {{ m.field(form.login, invalidFields) }}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.password.first) }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.password.second) }}</div>
        </div>
        {{ m.field(form.current_password) }}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ 'PERSONS.SAVE'|trans }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ path('area') }}">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.BACK'|trans }}</a>
        </div>
      {{ form_end(form) }}
    </div>

    {# 2. deletion. The password field has the same NAME as that of the first
       form (current_password), but another id: two elements of the same
       page cannot have the same id #}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_TITLE'|trans }}</h5>

“Manage my account”: two independent forms on the same page.

  • Lines 18–38: the update, using the [MyAccountType] form: the identity fields, the login, the new password and its confirmation (optional), and the current password (required). The version (optimistic lock) is set by [form_end];
  • Lines 43–56: Account deletion, a handwritten form with its own current password field and a confirmation field. The field is named [current_password] (the field in the first form is named [my_account[current_password]]: the Form component prefixes its field names with the form name), and its own unique ID: two elements on a page cannot have the same ID, as indicated by the [for] attribute of a label.
